items.title: The one-body reduction trace law of the finite-mode permutation sectors
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $n\ge1$, let $H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold
completed tensor power with $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$, let $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
be the permutation unitaries and let
$P_\sigma^{(n)}$, $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, be the sector projections
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), with sector space
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq H^{\otimes n}.$$
For $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
be the operator of clause (a) below, and put
$$\Sigma(O):=\sum_{i=1}^n O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n}).$$
Identify $H^{\otimes n}$ with $H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$ by the
surjective linear isometry $J_n$ of clause (b) below, and let
$\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}$ be the partial trace of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-finite-partial-trace-and-schmidt]] clause (a) over the
second factor of that identification. Then:

(a) *slot operators*: for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and every
$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ there is a unique $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
with $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{i-1}\otimes Ov_i\otimes v_{i+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$
for all $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$; it satisfies $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$ and
$(O^*)^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$; in particular $O=O^*$ gives $O^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$;

(b) *parenthesisation*: the assignment
$v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\mapsto v_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)$
extends to a surjective linear isometry
$J_n:H^{\otimes n}\to H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$;

(c) *permutation invariance*: $U_\pi\,\Sigma(O)\,U_\pi^*=\Sigma(O)$ for every
$\pi\in S_n$; consequently $\Sigma(O)$ preserves both sector spaces and commutes with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$:
$$\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)};$$

(d) *trace law*: for every density operator $\rho$ on the sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]
clause (a)), with zero extension $\widetilde\rho:=P_\sigma^{(n)}\rho P_\sigma^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
obtained by regarding $\rho$ as an endomorphism of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$, and
for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=n\,\operatorname{tr}(\gamma\,O)$,
where $\gamma:=J_n^{-1}\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}(J_n\widetilde\rho\,J_n^{-1})\bigr)J_n$;

(e) *the reduced operator is a density operator*: the operator $\gamma$ of
clause (d) is a density operator on $H$; it is independent of the choice of
slot in the sense that it equals the partial trace of $\widetilde\rho$ over
the other $n-1$ slots in the parenthesisation in which the retained slot is
the one the display names;

(f) *scope*: clauses (a)-(e) are exact operator identities on the
finite-dimensional labelled tensor powers; no physical system, particle
species, preparation or measurement is asserted, and the parameter $n$ is a
dimension count of the construction, not an observed particle number.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$ of dimension $d\ge1$, the integer $n\ge1$, the completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$ with permutation unitaries $U_\pi$ and sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$, the operator $O\in\mathcal B(H)$, the slot index $i$, and the density operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ with its zero extension $\widetilde\rho$.

[F1] **Tensor powers.** $H^{\otimes n}$ is a complex Hilbert space; the elementary tensors have dense linear span; $\|v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\|=\|v_1\|\cdots\|v_n\|$ and $\langle v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n,w_1\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n\rangle=\prod_{k}\langle v_k,w_k\rangle$; for orthonormal families spanning $H$ the corresponding elementary tensors form an orthonormal family with dense span ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clauses (b), (c), (d)).

[F2] **Parenthesisation.** For every parenthesisation the iterated tensor product represents multilinear maps, and different parenthesisations are connected by the unique isomorphism preserving pure tensors ([[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]).

[F3] **Bounded tensor maps.** For $S,T\in\mathcal B(H)$ there is a unique $S\otimes T\in\mathcal B(H\widehat\otimes H)$ with $(S\otimes T)(u\otimes v)=Su\otimes Tv$, $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$, $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$, and for endomorphisms $S\otimes I$ and $I\otimes T$ commute ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F4] **Permutation unitaries and sectors.** $U_\pi$ is unitary with $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n)}$ and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$; $U_\pi P_+^{(n)}=P_+^{(n)}U_\pi=P_+^{(n)}$ and $U_\pi P_-^{(n)}=P_-^{(n)}U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-^{(n)}$; the range of $P_+^{(n)}$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-^{(n)}$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F5] **Partial trace.** For endomorphisms $R$ of $V\otimes W$ with $V,W$ finite-dimensional, there is a unique endomorphism $\operatorname{Tr}_W R$ of $V$ with $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_WR)A)=\operatorname{tr}(R(A\otimes I_W))$ for every $A\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, independent of the orthonormal basis used in its construction; if $R\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}R=1$ then $\operatorname{Tr}_WR\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_WR=1$ ([[thm-nrqm-composites-finite-partial-trace-and-schmidt]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F6] **Density operators.** A density operator on a nonzero complex Hilbert space is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator of trace one ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a), [[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]).

[F7] **Trace laws.** The trace of an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space is basis independent, linear, and $\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{tr}(YX)$ ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]], [[prop-trace-is-linear]]); for a trace-class operator $T$ and bounded $S$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(ST)=\operatorname{tr}(TS)$ ([[thm-cyclicity-of-the-trace]]).

[F8] **Agreement on dense sets.** Two bounded linear operators from a normed space into a Banach space that agree on a dense subspace are equal ([[thm-extension-of-a-bounded-map-from-a-dense-subspace]]).

[F9] **Unitary conjugation preserves the operator norm.** If $U$ is unitary then $\|UTU^*\|=\|T\|$ ([[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; construct the slot operators by conjugating the first-slot tensor map with a permutation unitary, transport the partial trace through the parenthesisation isometry, and reduce every slot to the first by permutation invariance and cyclicity.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F9].

1.1 [The parenthesisation isometry] The map $(v_1,\dots,v_n)\mapsto v_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)$ is multilinear from $H^n$ into $H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$, so by [F2] applied to the two parenthesisations of the $n$-fold algebraic tensor product it defines a linear map on the algebraic tensor product, and this linear map preserves inner products on elementary tensors by [F1]: $\langle v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n,w_1\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n\rangle=\prod_k\langle v_k,w_k\rangle=\langle v_1,w_1\rangle\langle v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n,w_2\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n\rangle$. Since the elementary tensors span a dense subspace and both sides are complete, [F8] and this isometry identity give a linear isometry $J_n$ on the completed tensor powers, and the image is closed and contains all elementary tensors $v_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)$, whose span is dense by [F1]; hence $J_n$ is surjective. This proves (b). [F1, F2, F8, algebra]

1.2 [The first-slot operator] By [F3] the operator $O\otimes I_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}\in\mathcal B(H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)})$ is bounded with $(O\otimes I)(u\otimes w)=Ou\otimes w$. Transporting it through the isometry $J_n$ of clause (b) gives a bounded operator $A_1:=J_n^{-1}(O\otimes I)J_n$ on $H^{\otimes n}$ with $A_1(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=J_n^{-1}(Ov_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n))=Ov_1\otimes v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$ for all $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$. [F1, F3, algebra]

1.3 [The zero extension and its symmetry] Regard $\rho$ as an endomorphism of $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ and put $\widetilde\rho:=P_\sigma^{(n)}\rho P_\sigma^{(n)}$, an endomorphism of $H^{\otimes n}$ whose restriction to $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is $\rho$ and which vanishes on the orthogonal complement; then $\widetilde\rho\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}\widetilde\rho=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ by [F6] and [F7], so $\widetilde\rho$ is a density operator on $H^{\otimes n}$ with $\widetilde\rho=P_\sigma^{(n)}\widetilde\rho P_\sigma^{(n)}$. Since $U_\pi$ preserves $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ and acts on it as the scalar $\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)$ by [F4], $U_\pi\widetilde\rho U_\pi^*=\widetilde\rho$ for every $\pi$. [F4, F6, F7, algebra]

2.1 [Slot operators and the permutation invariance of their sum] Fix $i$, choose $\pi\in S_n$ with $\pi(1)=i$ and set $O^{(i)}:=U_\pi A_1U_\pi^*\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$; [F9] and step 1.2 give $\|O^{(i)}\|=\|O\otimes I\|\le\|O\|$, and [F3], [F4] give $(O^{(i)})^*=U_\pi(O^*\otimes I)U_\pi^*=(O^*)^{(i)}$, so $O=O^*$ gives $O^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$. On elementary tensors, [F4] gives $U_\pi^*(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi(n)}$; step 1.2 replaces the first factor by $Ov_{\pi(1)}=Ov_i$; and $U_\pi$ then moves that factor to slot $\pi(1)=i$, leaving every other factor in its original slot, so $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes Ov_i\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$. If $\pi'$ is another permutation with $\pi'(1)=i$, then $\tau:=\pi^{-1}\pi'$ fixes $1$ and $U_\tau A_1U_\tau^*$ agrees with $A_1$ on elementary tensors by [F1], [F3], hence equals it by [F8]; thus $U_{\pi'}A_1U_{\pi'}^*=U_\pi U_\tau A_1U_\tau^*U_\pi^*=U_\pi A_1U_\pi^*$ and $O^{(i)}$ is well defined, with the displayed elementary-tensor action. For $\tau\in S_n$ one then has $U_\tau O^{(i)}U_\tau^*=U_{\tau\pi}A_1U_{\tau\pi}^*=O^{(\tau(i))}$, and summing over $i$ with $\tau$ permuting $\{1,\dots,n\}$ gives $U_\tau\Sigma(O)U_\tau^*=\Sigma(O)$ for $\Sigma(O):=\sum_{i=1}^nO^{(i)}$; equivalently $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with every $U_\tau$. Since $P_\sigma^{(n)}=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)U_\pi$ is a finite linear combination of the $U_\pi$ by [F4], $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$, so it preserves $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ and its orthogonal complement and $\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)}$; this proves (a) and (c). [F1, F3, F4, F8, F9, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Reduction to one slot, the trace law and the reduced operator] Fix $i$ and $\pi$ with $\pi(1)=i$; by steps 1.3 and 2.1 and [F7], $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho O^{(i)})=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho U_\pi A_1U_\pi^*)=\operatorname{tr}(U_\pi^*\widetilde\rho U_\pi A_1)=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho A_1)$, where the middle equality is cyclicity and the last uses $U_\pi^*\widetilde\rho U_\pi=\widetilde\rho$. Therefore $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho O^{(i)})=n\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho A_1)=n\operatorname{tr}((O\otimes I)J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1})=n\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1})O)$ by [F7], [F5] and the explicit form of $A_1$ in step 1.2; with the definition of $\gamma$ this is (d). By [F5] clause (b) applied with $R=J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1}$, which is positive of trace one by step 1.3, the operator $\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1}$ is positive of trace one, so its conjugate $\gamma$ is a density operator on $H$. If instead another named slot is retained, the same computation with the corresponding slot operator produces $\gamma'$ with $n\operatorname{tr}((\gamma'-\gamma)O)=0$ for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$, hence $\gamma'=\gamma$ on testing against the rank-one operators $O=T_{u,v}$, for which $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma T_{u,v})=\langle\gamma u,v\rangle$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]); this proves (e) as well. [F5, F7, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion and scope] Step 1.1 proves (b), step 2.1 proves (a) and (c), and step 3.1 proves (d) and (e); every argument used only the finite-dimensional tensor construction, the permutation sectors, the partial trace and the trace axioms, and no physical object, preparation or measurement entered, which is clause (f). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Reading of the identities.** The law $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=n\operatorname{tr}(\gamma O)$ says that the mean of the sum of one-body slot operators in the sector preparation is $n$ times the trace pairing of a single one-particle operator with a reduced operator $\gamma$ on the one-particle space. Only the identity is asserted here; its physical reading requires the framework postulates and a declared preparation, and is stated separately.
- **Why the factor $n$ appears.** The sum $\Sigma(O)$ has $n$ slot terms with equal pairings by permutation invariance of the sector state, and $\gamma$ is normalised once, $\operatorname{tr}\gamma=1$; the factor $n$ is the multiplicity of the sum, not a further normalisation.

items.title: Closed formulas for the two-level canonical weights, mean energy, entropy and free energy
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\varepsilon>0$ and $\beta>0$ be real parameters, let $\mathfrak h$ be a
two-dimensional complex Hilbert space with orthonormal basis
$(u_0,u_1)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
and let $H:=T_{u_1,u_1}\varepsilon=\varepsilon\,T_{u_1,u_1}$ be the
self-adjoint operator with eigenvalues $0$ on $\mathbb Cu_0$ and
$\varepsilon$ on $\mathbb Cu_1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]). Let
$$Z:=\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j},\qquad \rho_\beta:=\frac1Z\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j}T_{u_j,u_j},\qquad s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i$$
be the partition sum, canonical operator and entropy of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause
(a), with $E_0=0$, $E_1=\varepsilon$ and $w_i$ the eigenvalues of a density
operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak h$ ([[def-natural-logarithm]]). Then:

(a) $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\in(1,2)$, and
$$\rho_\beta=\frac1Z\bigl(T_{u_0,u_0}+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}T_{u_1,u_1}\bigr)$$
is a density operator on $\mathfrak h$ that is not the maximally mixed state
$\tfrac12\mathrm{id}$;

(b) the mean energy is the exact identity
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\frac{\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{Z}=\frac{\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1},\qquad 0<\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2};$$

(c) the entropy and free energy satisfy
$$s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z+\frac{\beta\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}=\log\bigl(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\bigr)+\frac{\beta\varepsilon\,e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}},\qquad 0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log 2,$$
and, with $F:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=F ;$$

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) are exact algebraic identities for the
declared two-dimensional Hilbert space and the two real parameters
$\varepsilon,\beta>0$; no temperature, thermodynamic, equilibrium or
measurement interpretation is asserted, and the parameter $\beta$ carries no
physical dimension in this lemma.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the real parameters $\varepsilon>0$, $\beta>0$, the two-dimensional complex Hilbert space $\mathfrak h$ with orthonormal basis $(u_0,u_1)$, the operator $H=\varepsilon T_{u_1,u_1}$, and the data $Z$, $\rho_\beta$, $s$ of the statement.

[F1] **Supplied finite Gibbs data.** For the finite-dimensional self-adjoint $H$ with real eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_d$ and orthonormal eigenbasis $(v_1,\dots,v_d)$, and $\beta>0$, one has $Z=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}\in(0,\infty)$ and $\rho_\beta=Z^{-1}\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}T_{v_j,v_j}\in\mathcal D$, with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=Z^{-1}\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}E_j$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$, and for every density operator $\rho$ one has $s(\rho)\le\log d$, with equality if and only if $\rho=d^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F2] **Rank-one calculus.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is bounded with $T_{u,v}^*=T_{v,u}$, $T_{x,x}\ge0$, $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$, and for bounded $B$ one has $BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v}$ and $T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^*v}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (a)-(d)); the trace is linear ([[prop-trace-is-linear]]) and $\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{tr}(YX)$ ([[thm-cyclicity-of-the-trace]]).

[F3] **Real exponential.** $\exp(x)>0$, $\exp(-x)=1/\exp(x)$, and $\exp(x+y)=\exp(x)\exp(y)$ for all real $x,y$ ([[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-exponential-addition-formula]]); $\exp$ is strictly increasing on $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]]). Hence $\exp(0)=\exp(0)^2$ with $\exp(0)>0$, so $\exp(0)=1$, and $\exp(t)>\exp(0)=1$ for every $t>0$.

[F4] **Logarithm.** $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$ and satisfies $\log(xy)=\log x+\log y$, $\log(1/x)=-\log x$ and $\log 1=0$ ([[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the supplied finite Gibbs formulas at the two eigenvalues $0,\varepsilon$, and control the exponential factor at $\beta\varepsilon>0$ with strict increase, positivity and the reciprocal law.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Exponential comparison] Since $\beta\varepsilon>0$, strict increase in [F3] gives $\exp(\beta\varepsilon)>\exp(0)=1$, and [F3] gives $\exp(-\beta\varepsilon)=1/\exp(\beta\varepsilon)\in(0,1)$; consequently $1<Z=1+\exp(-\beta\varepsilon)<2$. [F3, algebra]

2.1 [The canonical operator] By [F1] with $E_0=0$, $E_1=\varepsilon$ and $(v_1,v_2)=(u_0,u_1)$, $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$ and $\rho_\beta=Z^{-1}(T_{u_0,u_0}+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}T_{u_1,u_1})\in\mathcal D$, so $\rho_\beta$ is a density operator; its two weights are $Z^{-1}$ and $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}Z^{-1}$, which are distinct because $\exp(-\beta\varepsilon)\ne1$ by step 1.1. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Mean energy, entropy and free energy] Using [F2] and $T_{u_0,u_0}T_{u_1,u_1}=T_{u_0,u_1}$ with $\langle u_1,u_0\rangle=0$, and $T_{u_1,u_1}T_{u_1,u_1}=T_{u_1,u_1}$ with $\langle u_1,u_1\rangle=1$, the product $\rho_\beta H$ equals $\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}Z^{-1}T_{u_1,u_1}$, so [F2] gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/Z$; by step 1.1, $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/Z=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon})=1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)$, hence $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\varepsilon/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)$ lies in $(0,\varepsilon/2)$. By [F1], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$, so $s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z+\beta\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\log(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon})+\beta\varepsilon/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)=\log(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon})+\beta\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon})$; by [F1] and [F2], $0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log2$ because $\rho_\beta\ne\tfrac12\mathrm{id}$ by step 2.1. Finally $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z=F$ with $F$ as defined. This proves (b) and (c), and step 2.1 proved (a). [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion] Steps 1.1-2.1 prove (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and (c), and every identity is an algebraic consequence of the supplied finite-dimensional formulas and the real exponential and logarithm laws, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **High- and low-temperature expectations.** By [F3], $0<e^{-\beta\varepsilon}<1$ and $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$ decreases strictly as the product $\beta\varepsilon$ grows, so the upper level is suppressed in the regime of large $\beta\varepsilon$, while the bound $s<\log2$ of clause (c) shows that the entropy stays below the maximal mixed-state value for every finite $\beta>0$. The lemma asserts only these algebraic facts about the weights; it identifies no physical temperature with $\beta$.
- **Use.** The formulas are the exact two-level data used by the examples and the thought experiment of the companion page; the physical reading of $\beta$ as an inverse temperature, and of $\rho_\beta$ as a thermal preparation, is supplied separately by the framework's equilibrium postulate.

items.title: The declared fixed-N many-body model: species sector, one-particle data, interaction and the sector energy observable
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings, units and choice hypotheses.** Adopt the state and
composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the
observable and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4), the non-relativistic kinematics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] (P5)
and the identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), in the state
reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable
reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
evolution reading of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
the sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]].
Let a **declared species sector** with one-particle space $H$, mass $m>0$
(kg), spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and statistics choice
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$ be given as in that definition, in the massive spin-$s$
one-particle reading of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; fix an integer
$N\ge1$ and let $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}\subseteq
H^{\otimes N}$ be the declared $N$-particle sector. All quantities below are
read in the SI conventions and units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (energies in joules). Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]); the Axiom of Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) is assumed only in the Coulomb realization of
clause (d)(ii), where it is the choice hypothesis of the cited self-adjointness
theorem.

**(b) Declared one-particle data.** The model declares a one-particle
**energy operator** in one of the two following realizations.

(i) *Spatial realization.* The one-particle space is
$H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and, with $\hbar>0$ the reduced Planck
constant, the model declares a **kinetic operator** $K_1:=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta$
on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and a real, measurable, bounded
**external potential** $V_{\mathrm{ext}}:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ of essential
supremum $\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}\|_\infty<\infty$; the declared one-particle
operator is $h:=K_1+V_{\mathrm{ext}}(Q)$ with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$. A more singular declared
$V_{\mathrm{ext}}$, such as $-g/|x|$, is used only through a separate
self-adjointness statement, which the model must supply before the operator is
read as an observable.

(ii) *Finite-mode realization.* A finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space
$K$ of dimension $d\ge1$ with a declared orthonormal basis
$(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) is declared together with a
self-adjoint **one-particle operator** $h\in\mathcal B(K)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).
Here the one-particle space of the species is $K$, and the assignment of the
modes $f_j$ to a laboratory mode family is a tested identification under the
preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not part of the definition.

**(c) Declared interaction.** The model declares a **pair interaction** in the
matching realization.

(i) *Bounded interaction.* In the spatial realization let
$W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be real, measurable, bounded with
$W(-z)=W(z)$ for almost every $z$ and $\|W\|_\infty<\infty$. In the
finite-mode realization let $W\in\mathcal B(K\widehat\otimes K)$ be
self-adjoint with $U_{(12)}WU_{(12)}=W$, where $U_{(12)}$ is the exchange
unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clause (a)
in the tensor square $\widehat{K\otimes K}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. The interaction strength
constants entering $W$ are empirical model parameters with their uncertainties
in the sense of P6 clause (iii).

(ii) *Coulomb interaction.* In the spatial realization the model may declare
the singular pair interaction $W(z):=\kappa/|z|$ with a real coupling
$\kappa\in\mathbb R$ (repulsive for $\kappa>0$), and an external
$V_{\mathrm{ext}}(x):=-g/|x|$ with $g\in\mathbb R$; the combined singular
multiplier is that of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]].

**(d) The labelled energy operator and its sector restriction.** Fix the
particle masses $m_1=\cdots=m_N=m$ of the declared species.

(i) *Spatial, bounded case.* With $\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)^{\otimes N}\to L^2(\mathbb R^{3N})$
the Euclidean product unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], form the labelled
operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=K+M_W$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] clause (b)
whose potential is
$V(X)=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W(x_i-x_j)$; by that theorem
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
and bounded below by $-\|V\|_\infty$. By clause (e) of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] the
transported projections $\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}$ reduce
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$, and the restriction
$$H_N^\sigma:=\bigl(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}\bigr)H_{\mathrm{lab}}\bigl(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1}\bigr)\big|_{\operatorname{ran}(\Theta P_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta^{-1})}$$
is a self-adjoint operator on the transported sector; the model identifies it
with the restriction of $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ to
$\Theta^{-1}$-transported $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in the tensor reading.

(ii) *Spatial Coulomb case.* With the singular data of clause (c)(ii), the
operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=K+M_V$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]] clause (b)
is self-adjoint with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and
bounded below, and by clause (d) of that theorem its restrictions to the
symmetric and antisymmetric sectors are self-adjoint; the model's sector
energy operator $H_N^\sigma$ is that restriction, with the same reading as in
(i).

(iii) *Finite-mode case.* On $K^{\otimes N}$ put
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=\sum_{i=1}^N h^{(i)}+\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}W^{(ij)},$$
where $h^{(i)}$ is the slot operator of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (the identity on all factors but
the $i$-th, $h$ on the $i$-th) and $W^{(ij)}$ is the transport of
$W\in\mathcal B(K\widehat\otimes K)$ to the pair of slots $(i,j)$ by any
permutation moving that pair to the first two slots; the symmetry
$U_{(12)}WU_{(12)}=W$ makes the order of the pair immaterial and
$W\otimes I$ commutes with permutations fixing the first two slots, so the
transported operator is independent of the permutation chosen. Then
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is bounded and self-adjoint,
it commutes with every permutation unitary, and the model's sector energy
operator is $H_N^\sigma:=H_{\mathrm{lab}}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}=P_\sigma^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}P_\sigma^{(N)}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$.

**(e) The model's energy reading and evolution.** In every realization the
pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is declared to be the **assigned energy
observable** of the $N$-particle sector in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a): its
outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is the law
$\mu^{H_N^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$ of that
definition clause (b), and its spectral data are those of the self-adjoint
operator constructed in clause (d). The **model evolution** is the unitary
flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b) with this
generator. The identification of the operator with the energy of a concrete
sample, and the assignment of numerical masses, couplings and potentials to a
laboratory species, are tested identifications with uncertainty under P7;
they are not consequences of P1-P6.

**(f) The non-interacting reading.** The model is called **non-interacting**
when $W=0$ (equivalently $\kappa=0$), so that
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_{i=1}^Nh^{(i)}$; in the spatial realization this is the
case $V=V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ summed over slots of the bounded-fixed-$N$ theorem.

**(g) Scope.** The declared model is a kinematic and dynamical input of this
pair: it fixes a state space, a sector, an energy operator and an evolution,
and nothing else. It asserts no stability of matter, no Hunziker-van
Winter-Zhislin threshold statement, no statement about excited threshold
structure, no thermodynamic limit, no equilibration or thermalization, no
measured energy and no identification of its parameters with a particular
laboratory sample beyond the tested identifications of P7. The finite-mode
realization is an idealization confining the one-particle content to $d$
declared modes; the spatial realization is an idealization of an $N$-particle
non-relativistic sample with the declared external field and pair interaction.

## Remarks

- **Why the sector restriction is legitimate.** In the spatial realizations
  the permutation unitaries preserve the domain $W^{2,2}$ and commute with
  $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$, which is exactly the hypothesis of the
  permutation-restricted self-adjointness theorem; in the finite-mode
  realization the bounded operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ commutes with the
  $U_\pi$ by construction, and a bounded operator commuting with a projection
  restricts to a self-adjoint operator on its range.
- **Units.** $m$ is in kg, $\hbar$ in J s, $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ and $\|V\|_\infty$
  in J, $W$ in J and $\kappa$ in J m; in the finite-mode realization $h$ and
  $W$ are declared directly in joules. No magnetic coupling, spin-orbit term or
  velocity-dependent interaction is part of this model.

Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 6.1 and 10.1-10.2 printed pages 104-111 and 226-235 (PDF pages 112-119 and 234-243): composite systems, the non-interacting composite Hamiltonian, the antisymmetric electron-pair wavefunction and the two-electron Hamiltonian with the mutual electrostatic repulsion term (10.24a)

F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Chapter 1 Sections 1.1, 1.2 and 1.4 pp. 3-13: systems of independent particles, the occupation-number representation, Fock space and the second-quantised form of one- and two-body operators (equations (46)-(48) and Section 1.4.3)

items.title: The declared one-body reduced operator and the one-body readout of a sector preparation
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the observable and
probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2)
in the state reading of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the observable reading
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]. Work in the
**finite-mode realization** of a declared species sector of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]:
the one-particle space is a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $K$ of
dimension $d\ge1$ with its declared orthonormal modes $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, and
the $N$-particle sector space is
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}\subseteq K^{\otimes N}$
with the declared sector preparations of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) The one-body reduced operator.** Let $\rho$ be a declared sector
preparation, that is, a density operator on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).
The **one-body reduced preparation** of $\rho$ is the density operator
$\gamma_\rho$ on $K$ of clause (e) of
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-one-body-reduction-trace-law]] (with $H:=K$, $n:=N$ and
the same sector projections); it is the partial trace of $\rho$ over $N-1$
of the labelled factors. By that lemma $\gamma_\rho$ is a density operator
on $K$ independent of which factor is traced, and for every
$O\in\mathcal B(K)$ the pairings are related by
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O)\bigr)=N\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\gamma_\rho\,O\bigr),$$
where $\widetilde\rho$ is the zero extension of $\rho$ and $\Sigma(O)$ is the
sum over the $N$ labelled slots of the slot operator $O^{(i)}$.

**(c) The one-body readout.** For a declared **bounded self-adjoint**
$O\in\mathcal B(K)$ with a declared unit $u_O$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], the model reads the sector
operator
$$A_O:=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}=P_\sigma^{(N)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$$
as an **assigned sharp observable** $(A_O,u_O)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a): it
is bounded and self-adjoint on the nonzero sector space and its outcome law
in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is the law
$\mu^{A_O}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A_O}(B))$ of clause (b) of that
definition. The **one-body readout** of $O$ in $\rho$ is the mean of that law
when it exists.

**(d) Scope.** The reduced preparation $\gamma_\rho$ is a mathematical
partial trace of the sector state; it is not asserted to be the state of any
individual particle, and it does not determine the sector preparation $\rho$:
many sector preparations have the same one-body reduction. The definition
asserts no separability or factorization of $\rho$, no result for the spatial
(infinite-dimensional) realization, whose reduction would require the
separable partial trace, and no measurement of individual particle labels,
which are mathematical factor labels by P6 clause (i). Whether a declared
laboratory preparation realizes a sector preparation $\rho$ and a quantity
realizes the pair $(A_O,u_O)$ are tested identifications with uncertainty
under P7, not consequences of this definition.

## Remarks

- **Normalization.** The one-body reduced preparation is normalized as a
  probability state, $\operatorname{tr}\gamma_\rho=1$, while the mean of the
  sum $A_O$ carries the factor $N$; the sum $\Sigma(O)$ is a many-body
  quantity, not a single-particle quantity, and its mean is $N$ times the
  single-particle pairing with $\gamma_\rho$.
- **Choice of retained factor.** Lemma clause (e) shows that reducing over
  any $N-1$ of the labelled factors gives the same operator on $K$; this is
  the precise sense in which the reduction is label independent inside the
  model.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 6.1-6.3 printed pages 105-126 (PDF pages 113-134): composite systems, local operators A tensor I, the reduced density operator obtained by tracing out one factor, and its use for local predictions
F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Section 1.4.2 pp. 8-10: single-particle operators (46)-(48) as sums of slot operators in the occupation-number representation

items.title: Entropy, the Boltzmann constant and the free-energy functional of the declared finite-sector model
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings and restricted sector class.** Adopt the observable and
probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2)
and the autonomous-dynamics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], for the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]. This definition
applies to the class of declared models whose sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is **finite-dimensional**, in particular to every
finite-mode realization
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]]), where
$D:=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is finite by
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a),
(b). Write $\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$ for the set of declared sector
preparations, that is, the density operators on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) Dimensionless entropy.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$
with eigenvalues $w_1,\dots,w_D\ge0$ (counted with multiplicity, in any
order), the **entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i\in[0,\log D],$$
the quantity of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]]
clause (a) with $\log$ the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]]). It is dimensionless, is a function of the
eigenvalue multiset of $\rho$ alone, and equals zero exactly for pure
preparations; by clause (c) of the cited theorem $s(\rho)=\log D$ holds
exactly when $\rho=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$.

**(c) Boltzmann constant, temperature and inverse temperature.** The model
assigns a positive **Boltzmann constant** $k_B$ and a positive **temperature**
$T$; in the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the unit of $k_B$ is
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$, the unit of $T$ is the kelvin, and
$$k_B=1.380\,649\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$$
fixed exactly by the BIPM SI definition. The model declares the **inverse
temperature** $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$, a positive real number in $\mathrm J^{-1}$.
The value and exactness of $k_B$ are unit-convention facts; the assignment of
the parameter $T$ to a physical sample, and the identification of
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ with an inverse thermodynamic temperature, are adopted
assumptions of the ensemble model of this pair, not consequences of P1-P4,
and are tested identifications with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus postulate P7.

**(d) Physical entropy.** The **physical entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$S(\rho):=k_B\,s(\rho),$$
read in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$. It is nonnegative, is at most
$k_B\log D$, and vanishes exactly for pure preparations.

**(e) Free-energy functional.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$,
let $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)\in\mathbb R$ be the mean of the
declared energy observable in $\rho$ (finite because $D<\infty$, in the
moment reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).
The **Helmholtz free-energy reading** of $\rho$ is
$$F(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho),$$
read in joules; it is the quantity
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a)
at the identified $\beta$. For the canonical operator
$\rho_\beta:=e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}/Z_N$ and
$Z_N:=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}\in(0,\infty)$ (finite sum in the
finite-dimensional sector), the number $F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$
is called the **equilibrium free energy**; it is the value of the functional
at $\rho_\beta$ by the cited theorem.

**(f) Scope.** This definition covers only declared models with
finite-dimensional sector space and preparations in
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$. For a declared spatial realization, whose
sector space is infinite-dimensional, the operator $\rho\log\rho$ need not be
trace class; no entropy, physical entropy or free energy is defined here for
that case, and a separate trace-class statement would be required. The
definition asserts no increase of entropy in time, no equilibration to
$\rho_\beta$, no thermodynamic limit, no pressure or volume variable, and no
measured temperature, entropy or free energy.

## Remarks

- **Why the finite case first.** In the finite-dimensional sector the entropy
  is an ordinary finite sum over $D$ eigenvalues, and the comparison theorem
  of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] is
  available without any trace-class convergence hypothesis on
  $\rho\log\rho$. The infinite-dimensional questions are deferred rather than
  assumed.
- **Units of $\beta$.** $\beta=1/(k_BT)$ has the unit
  $\mathrm J^{-1}\mathrm K\,\mathrm K^{-1}=\mathrm J^{-1}$, so the exponent
  $\beta H_N^\sigma$ is dimensionless, as the spectral calculus requires.

references.title: BIPM, The International System of Units (SI), 9th edition 2019, Section 2.2 Table 1 printed pages 123-124 (PDF pages 12-13): the Boltzmann constant k is fixed to 1.380 649 x 10^-23 J K^-1 as an exact defining constant

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.3.2 printed pages 127-129 (PDF pages 135-137): the Shannon entropy s = -sum p_i ln p_i and its operator form -Tr(rho ln rho); Section 6.4 printed pages 129-131 (PDF pages 137-139): the Gibbs distribution, beta = 1/(k_B T), the thermodynamic entropy S = k_B s (6.98) and the Helmholtz free energy F = -k_B T ln Z (6.99)

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.3 printed pages 13-14: the von Neumann entropy S = -sum_j lambda_j ln lambda_j; Section 1.1.5 printed page 15: F = -T ln Z and F = E - T S

items.title: The canonical equilibrium-ensemble assumption: the Gibbs preparation of a declared model at assigned temperature
items.statement:
## Postulate

**(a) Adopted readings and framework data.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable
and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4) and the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7), together with a
declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] and the entropy,
Boltzmann-constant and free-energy vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Let
$H_N^\sigma$ be the model's sector energy operator with spectral
projection-valued measure $E$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), assume it is bounded below, let $T>0$ be
an assigned temperature in kelvin and let $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$ in
$\mathrm J^{-1}$ with the assigned Boltzmann constant $k_B$ of the entropy
definition. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral calculus.

**(b) Existence hypothesis and the Gibbs preparation.** Assume the
**partition sum is finite**:
$$Z_N:=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-\beta\lambda}\,d\bigl(\operatorname{tr}E(\lambda)\bigr)<\infty .$$
Then $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$ is defined by the spectral calculus of the
self-adjoint generator, it is positive with finite trace $Z_N>0$, and the
model adopts as the **canonical** or **Gibbs preparation** of the declared
model at temperature $T$ the density operator
$$\rho_\beta:=Z_N^{-1}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}.$$
In the finite-dimensional sector class of the entropy definition, $Z_N$ is
the finite sum $\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ over the eigenvalues and $\rho_\beta$
is the canonical operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]]; the
hypothesis $Z_N<\infty$ is automatic there. Outside that class the
hypothesis is a genuine restriction: the single-mode calculation of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] exhibits the
case $Z_N=(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$, and the product criterion of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]] shows that
countably many free modes have finite $Z_N$ exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$.

**(c) The equilibrium assumption and thermal means.** The model **assumes**
that, for a declared sample of the species at the assigned temperature $T$
and in the absence of further preparation information, the preparation
description of the sample is $\rho_\beta$ in the sense of P1. For an assigned
sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ of the system whose mean in $\rho_\beta$ exists
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)),
the number
$$\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)$$
is the model's **thermal mean** of $A$ at temperature $T$, read in the unit
$u_A$; when the mean does not exist the model asserts no thermal mean. The
identification of the parameter $T$ with the thermodynamic temperature of a
sample, and of $\beta$ with its inverse temperature, is part of this
assumption; the stated conservation and equilibrium properties of
$\rho_\beta$ under the flow of P4, and the extremal property of $\rho_\beta$
among preparations, are separate conditional results of this pair.

**(d) Motivation and status.** The assumption is motivated, but not
established, by the maximum-entropy reasoning of the cited sources: among
preparations with a prescribed mean energy, the Gibbs weights maximize the
entropy functional, and the finite-dimensional comparison theorem makes
$\rho_\beta$ the minimizer of the free-energy functional. That reasoning is
an argument inside mathematical statistics and thermodynamics; it does not
derive the physical assumption that a sample is described by $\rho_\beta$.
The postulate is an **adopted** statistical-mechanical assumption of the
model, in the sense of the content model's distinction between adopted
assumptions and derived consequences.

**(e) Scope.** The postulate asserts nothing about how a sample reaches the
Gibbs preparation; in particular it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration
time, no ergodicity, no master-equation or Markov approximation, no
thermodynamic limit, no pressure, volume or phase-transition structure, and
no measured temperature or expectation. The requirement $Z_N<\infty$ is part
of the assumption; the model does not define a canonical preparation when the
partition sum diverges. Any comparison with a laboratory sample requires the
declared preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7, and
agreement of a thermal prediction with data is evidence about the combined
model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework or of this
postulate.

## Remarks

- **The finite-sector case.** For a finite-dimensional sector the existence
  hypothesis is a finite sum and hence automatic; the only content of clause
  (b) there is the assignment of the Gibbs weights to the declared energies.
- **Relation to P4.** The postulate adds a preparation assumption to the
  dynamics; by itself P4 describes the unitary evolution of whatever
  preparation is declared, and does not single out $\rho_\beta$. The precise
  sense in which unitary evolution cannot produce $\rho_\beta$ from a
  different preparation is a separate theorem of this pair.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.4 printed pages 129-131 (PDF pages 137-139): the maximum-entropy motivation, the Gibbs distribution rho = Z^{-1} sum e^{-beta E_i}|i><i| (6.94), beta = 1/(k_B T) and Z = sum e^{-beta E_i} (6.93a,b), U = Tr(H rho) (6.95) and S = k_B s (6.98)

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.2 printed page 13: the Gibbs distribution rho = e^{-beta H}/Z, Z = Tr e^{-beta H}, with beta a formal inverse-energy parameter; Section 1.1.4 printed pages 14-15: the maximal-entropy principle and the free energy F = -T ln Z

items.title: Diagonalisation of the non-interacting finite-mode sector: occupation eigenvalues, partition sum and ground energy
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]),
the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) and the identical-particle and
spin postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in
the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]: one-particle space
$K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with declared modes $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$,
particle number $N\ge1$, sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, one-particle
self-adjoint operator $h\in\mathcal B(K)$, and **non-interacting** interaction
$W=0$, so that $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_{i=1}^Nh^{(i)}$ and
$H_N^\sigma=H_{\mathrm{lab}}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ in the notation of that
definition. Let $e_1,\dots,e_d$ be an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of
$h$ with real eigenvalues $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_d$ and let
$\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\cdots\le\varepsilon_{(d)}$ be the nondecreasing
rearrangement of the list. Then:

(a) *the labelled operator is diagonal*: $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is bounded and
self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$, it commutes with every
permutation unitary $U_\pi$, and for every multi-index
$i=(i_1,\dots,i_N)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^N$,
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}\,(e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N})=\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{i_k}\Bigr)e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N};$$

(b) *occupation eigenvalues and spectrum*: for every $N$-element subset
$J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ the Slater vector $e_J^\wedge$ of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (b) is an
eigenvector of $H_N^-$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_J:=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j$,
and for every occupation vector $\lambda\in W(N,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$
the symmetric vector $m_\lambda$ of clause (c) is an eigenvector of
$H_N^+$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_\lambda:=\sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j\varepsilon_j$;
the families $(e_J^\wedge)$ and $(m_\lambda)$ are orthogonal bases of
$\mathfrak H_N^-$ and $\mathfrak H_N^+$ respectively, so the spectrum of
$H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of these eigenvalues (with multiplicities
given by the number of configurations producing them); for $\sigma=-$ and
$N>d$ the sector space is $\{0\}$ and the model has no sector states;

(c) *partition sum and ground energy*: for every $\beta>0$ the number
$$Z_N(\beta):=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}=\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in W(N,d)\\ \lambda_j\le1\ \text{if }\sigma=-}}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$$
is a finite sum with $0<Z_N(\beta)<\infty$, bounded by the number of
occupation configurations; if $\sigma=-$ and $N\le d$ the ground eigenvalue
is $E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ and if $\sigma=+$ it is
$E_0=N\varepsilon_{(1)}$, and for every unit vector $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
one has $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_0$, with equality exactly on
the eigenspace of $E_0$;

(d) *reading and stationarity*: the pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is the
model's assigned energy observable; in a declared sector preparation $\rho$
its outcome law is $\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$,
and in the pure preparation of each sector basis vector of clause (b) this
law is the point mass at the displayed eigenvalue; each such vector is a
stationary state of the model evolution $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$, and
the energy law of every declared sector preparation is the law of the finite
spectral sum in the sector basis;

(e) *scope*: the theorem is conditional on the finite-mode idealization, on
the declared $h$ and on $W=0$; it asserts nothing for interacting models, for
spatial realizations, for infinite mode families, about thermal states or
equilibration, and about any laboratory system.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the finite-mode non-interacting model data of the statement with its eigenbasis $(e_1,\dots,e_d)$, eigenvalues $\varepsilon_j$, sector projections $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ and sector space $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$.

[F1] **Finite spectral theorem.** A self-adjoint endomorphism $h$ of the finite-dimensional complex inner product space $K$ is normal, so $K$ has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of $h$ with real eigenvalues ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], [[def-hilbert-space]]).

[F2] **Slot operators.** For $h\in\mathcal B(K)$ the slot operator $h^{(i)}$ acts on elementary tensors by $h^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes hv_i\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N$, is bounded with $\|h^{(i)}\|\le\|h\|$, and $(h^{(i)})^*=(h^*)^{(i)}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]).

[F3] **Product basis and occupation bases.** The elementary tensors $e_i=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ over all multi-indices form an orthonormal basis of $K^{\otimes N}$; the Slater vectors $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_N})$ over $N$-element subsets $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ form an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(N)}$ with $e_J^\wedge$ zero-free for distinct indices and vanishing on repeated indices; the vectors $m_\lambda=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$ over $\lambda\in W(N,d)$ form an orthogonal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(N)}$, and $N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)e_J^\wedge$, $N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_jm_\lambda$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]).

[F4] **Configuration counts.** The map $J\mapsto\mathbf 1_J$ is a bijection from $N$-element subsets onto $\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$, the sector dimensions are $\binom dN$ and $\binom{N+d-1}{N}$, and for $N>d$ the antisymmetric sector is $\{0\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a), (b), (c), [[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (b)).

[F5] **Stationary states.** For the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$, a nonzero $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ if and only if its pure preparation is stationary, and then $\psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi$ ([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (c)); the outcome law of an assigned observable in a preparation is the trace law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), and the trace is basis independent ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; expand in the product basis of one-particle eigenmodes, transport the diagonal action to the two sector bases, and read the finite spectrum and trace.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [The labelled operator on the product basis] By [F2] each $h^{(i)}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_ih^{(i)}$ is bounded and self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$. On the product basis vector $e_i=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ the $i$-th slot operator acts as $h$ on the factor $e_{i_k}$, giving $h^{(k)}e_i=\varepsilon_{i_k}e_i$; hence $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_k\varepsilon_{i_k})e_i$. Since every $U_\pi$ permutes the slots and $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is the sum over all slots, $U_\pi H_{\mathrm{lab}}U_\pi^*=H_{\mathrm{lab}}$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Sector eigenvectors] Let $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ and $i=(j_1,\dots,j_N)$. By [F3], $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i$; since $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ commutes with $P_-^{(N)}$ by step 1.1 and [F3], $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j)\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i=\lambda_Je_J^\wedge$. Likewise, for $\lambda\in W(N,d)$ and any multi-index $c$ with $|c|=\lambda$ one has $P_+^{(N)}e_c=\gamma_cm_\lambda$ with $\gamma_c>0$ by [F3], so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}m_\lambda=(\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j)m_\lambda$; because the $e_J^\wedge$ and the $m_\lambda$ are orthogonal bases of the respective sectors by [F3], [F4], the spectrum of $H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of the displayed eigenvalues with the configurations as multiplicities, and for $\sigma=-$, $N>d$ the sector is $\{0\}$. This proves (b). [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Partition sum and ground energy] The trace of $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$ is the sum of $e^{-\beta\lambda}$ over the eigenvalues with multiplicity, read on the orthogonal sector bases of step 2.1: $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{\lambda}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$ over the occupation configurations of clause (c), a finite nonempty sum of positive numbers for $\sigma=+$ and for $\sigma=-$ with $N\le d$, and empty (no sector states) for $\sigma=-$, $N>d$. If $\sigma=-$, then for every configuration $\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d$ with $\sum\lambda_j=N$ the support $J=\operatorname{supp}\lambda$ has $N$ elements and $\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j\ge\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ because the latter is the sum of the $N$ smallest eigenvalues; equality holds exactly for $J$ the set of indices of the $N$ smallest eigenvalues. If $\sigma=+$, then $\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j\ge\varepsilon_{(1)}\sum_j\lambda_j=N\varepsilon_{(1)}$, with equality exactly when every occupied mode has eigenvalue $\varepsilon_{(1)}$. Finally, expanding a unit $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in the orthogonal sector basis of step 2.1 gives $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2\lambda_\lambda\ge E_0$ with the stated equality case, where the coefficients are normalized. This proves (c). [F3, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 [Reading and stationarity] The pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is the model's assigned energy observable of clause (e) of the declared-model definition, so by [F5] its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is $\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$; for the pure preparation of a sector basis vector $\Psi$ of step 2.1, $E(\{\lambda\})\Psi=\Psi$ and hence $\mu_\Psi$ is the point mass at $\lambda$. By [F5] and step 2.1 each such $\Psi$ is an eigenvector of the generator, so its pure preparation is stationary under the flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ with $\Psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\Psi$, and the energy law of any preparation is the finite spectral law in the sector basis. This proves (d). [F5, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a) and (b), step 3.1 proves (c) and step 3.2 proves (d). The argument used the finite-mode idealization, the declared non-interacting $h$ and the finite-dimensional spectral and tensor calculus; no interaction, spatial realization, infinite mode family, thermal state, equilibration or laboratory identification entered, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Basis independence.** The eigenvalues $\lambda_J$ and $\lambda_\lambda$ depend on the eigenvalue list of $h$, not on the choice of eigenbasis; a degenerate one-particle eigenvalue contributes with its multiplicity through the distinct configurations.
- **Fermionic emptiness.** For $\sigma=-$ and $N>d$ the antisymmetric sector is zero, so the model as declared has no states and no energy observable; the theorem excludes that case in clauses (c), (d) rather than assigning it an energy.

items.title: The one-body readout law: sector means of summed bounded one-particle quantities and their reduced forms
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]])
and the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses
of the cited tensor, permutation and trace suppliers. Work in the finite-mode
realization of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-one-body-reduced-operator]]:
one-particle space $K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with modes
$(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, integer $N\ge1$ with nonzero sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, and the slot
operators $O^{(i)}$, sum $\Sigma(O)$ and one-body reduced preparation
$\gamma_\rho$ of that definition. Let $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ be self-adjoint
with declared unit $u_O$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) *the readout is an assigned observable*: the sector operator
$A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so the
pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the sector in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a);

(b) *the mean law*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ the mean of
the outcome law of $(A_O,u_O)$ in $\rho$ exists and equals
$$m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\gamma_\rho\,O\bigr);$$

(c) *product-type preparations*: if $u_1,\dots,u_N\in K$ are pairwise
orthonormal and $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\Psi:=S(u_1,\dots,u_N)$ the Slater
vector of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]]
clause (a) for $\sigma=-$, or $\Psi:=\sqrt{N!}\,P_+^{(N)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N)$
for $\sigma=+$ (both unit vectors of the sector), then
$\gamma_\rho=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NT_{u_j,u_j}$ and
$$m_\rho(A_O)=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle;$$

(d) *scope*: the theorem is conditional on the adopted sector of P6, on the
declared finite-mode idealization and on the declared preparation; it asserts
no measured mean, no property of an individual labelled particle, no
separability of $\rho$, no result for spatial infinite-mode models, and no
sampling or detection model. The equality $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$
is exact within the model.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the finite-mode sector data of the statement, the self-adjoint $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ with unit $u_O$, and a declared sector preparation $\rho$.

[F1] **Sector vocabulary.** $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is a closed subspace of $K^{\otimes N}$; every permutation unitary $U_\pi$ preserves it and acts there as the scalar $\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)$; a declared sector preparation is a density operator on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ ([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]] clauses (c)-(d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clause (c)).

[F2] **Slot operators and reduction.** For $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,N\}$ the slot operator $O^{(i)}$ satisfies $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes Ov_i\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N$, is bounded with $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$, and $(O^{(i)})^*=(O^*)^{(i)}$; $\Sigma(O)=\sum_iO^{(i)}$ commutes with every $U_\pi$ and with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$, preserves the sectors, and for every sector preparation $\rho$ with zero extension $\widetilde\rho$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$, where $\gamma_\rho$ is a density operator on $K$ ([[lem-nrqm-many-body-one-body-reduction-trace-law]] clauses (a), (c), (d), (e)).

[F3] **Observable reading and moments.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ has outcome law $\mu^A_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$; for a bounded self-adjoint $A$ and every preparation $\rho$ the mean exists and equals $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$, and for a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ it equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a), (b), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a), (d), [[prop-trace-is-linear]], [[thm-cyclicity-of-the-trace]]).

[F4] **Slater and symmetric product vectors.** For pairwise orthonormal $u_1,\dots,u_N$ the Slater vector $S(u_1,\dots,u_N)=N!^{-1/2}\sum_{\sigma\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)u_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{\sigma(N)}$ has norm one and equals $\sqrt{N!}\,P_-^{(N)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N)$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]] clauses (a), (b)); setting $x:=u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N$, orthonormality gives $\langle P_+^{(N)}x,x\rangle=\frac1{N!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_N}\langle U_\sigma x,x\rangle=\frac1{N!}\langle x,x\rangle=\frac1{N!}$, so $\Psi:=\sqrt{N!}\,P_+^{(N)}x$ is a unit vector of the symmetric sector with $P_+^{(N)}\Psi=\Psi$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clauses (b), (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]).

[F5] **Rank-one pairing.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is bounded with $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$ and $T_{u,v}^*=T_{v,u}$; the map $(u,v)\mapsto T_{u,v}$ is linear in $u$ and conjugate-linear in $v$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read the sector sum as a bounded observable, apply the supplied reduction identity, and evaluate the product-type cases by orthonormality of the mode family.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [The readout is a bounded self-adjoint sector observable] By [F2] each slot operator is bounded with $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$, so $\Sigma(O)$ is bounded with $\|\Sigma(O)\|\le N\|O\|$; since $O=O^*$, [F2] gives $O^{(i)*}=O^{(i)}$ for every $i$ and $\Sigma(O)^*=\Sigma(O)$. By [F2] $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$, hence preserves $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ and its orthogonal complement, and the restriction $A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator on the sector space; with the unit $u_O$ the pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is therefore an assigned sharp observable in the sense of [F3]. [F2, F3, def. bounded, algebra]

1.2 [Reduced preparation of product-type states] Let $u_1,\dots,u_N$ be pairwise orthonormal, put $x:=u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N$ and let $\Psi$ be the unit vector of clause (c) for $\sigma=-$ or $\sigma=+$; both satisfy $P_\sigma^{(N)}\Psi=\Psi$ by [F4], and both equal $\sqrt{N!}\,P_\sigma^{(N)}x$. Since $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ and $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is self-adjoint, $\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=N!\langle\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,P_\sigma^{(N)}x\rangle=N!\langle P_\sigma^{(N)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,x\rangle=N!\cdot\frac1{N!}\sum_{\tau\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\tau)\langle\Sigma(O)U_\tau x,x\rangle$, with $\operatorname{sgn}_+=1$ and $\operatorname{sgn}_-=\operatorname{sgn}$. For fixed $\tau$, $\langle\Sigma(O)U_\tau x,x\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^N\langle Ou_{\tau^{-1}(i)},u_i\rangle\prod_{k\ne i}\langle u_{\tau^{-1}(k)},u_k\rangle$ by [F1] and the elementary-tensor pairing, and orthonormality makes every factor $\delta_{\tau^{-1}(k),k}$ vanish unless $\tau=\mathrm{id}$; hence only the identity permutation contributes and $\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^N\langle Ou_i,u_i\rangle$. [F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 [The mean law] Let $\rho$ be a declared sector preparation with zero extension $\widetilde\rho$ and let $A_O$ be the readout of step 1.1. Since $A_O$ is bounded, [F3] gives $m_\rho(A_O)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A_O)$, and by steps 1.1 and [F2], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A_O)=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$. This proves (a) and (b). [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Product-type means and the reduced preparation] In the situation of step 1.2, the mean is $m_\rho(A_O)=\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle$, while the mean law of step 2.1 gives $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$. Testing the resulting identity $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle$ against $O=T_{u,v}$ and using [F5], $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho T_{u,v})=\langle\gamma_\rho u,v\rangle$ and $N^{-1}\sum_j\langle T_{u,v}u_j,u_j\rangle=N^{-1}\sum_j\langle u_j,v\rangle\langle u,u_j\rangle$; the identity for all $u,v$ therefore gives $\gamma_\rho=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NT_{u_j,u_j}$, since two endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional space with equal pairings against every rank-one operator are equal. This proves (c). [F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1-2.1 prove (a) and (b) and step 3.1 proves (c). Every quantity is a spectral datum of the declared finite-mode sector model and the argument used only P1, P2, P6 and the finite-dimensional tensor and trace calculus; no measured mean, individual-particle property, separability statement or spatial reduction entered, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **The factor $N$ and the normalization of $\gamma_\rho$.** The reduced preparation is normalized as a probability state on the one-particle space, while $A_O$ sums $N$ slot terms; the product-type case shows the two conventions consistently: a Slater determinant of $N$ orthonormal modes has reduced preparation the equal-weight mixture of those modes.
- **No separability claim.** The mean law holds for arbitrary sector preparations, entangled or not; nothing in the argument factors $\rho$, and the product-type clause is a special case.
