items.title: Direct and exchange contributions to a two-fermion mean energy and the repulsive-Coulomb ordering
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]),
the non-relativistic kinematics postulate P5
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]) and
the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]], and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Take a declared spin-$\tfrac12$ fermionic species
with mass $m>0$, the spatial realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] with $N=2$, a
bounded real external potential $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ and one of the following
two pair interactions: (bounded case) a bounded real even
$W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$; (Coulomb case) $W(z)=\kappa/|z|$ with
$\kappa>0$ and $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ bounded. Let $u,v\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
be pairwise orthonormal spatial orbitals, put
$$\varepsilon_u:=\langle u,h_1u\rangle_\star,\qquad \varepsilon_v:=\langle v,h_1v\rangle_\star$$
with $h_1$ the declared one-particle operator and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_\star$
the $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ pairing, and let $D$ and $X$ be the direct and
exchange integrals
$$D=\int_{\mathbb R^6}|u(x)|^2|v(y)|^2W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,\qquad X=\int_{\mathbb R^6}\overline{u(x)}v(x)u(y)\overline{v(y)}\,W(x-y)\,dx\,dy$$
of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]]
clause (c). Let $\chi_-$ be the spin singlet, $\chi_+$ the symmetric
$S_z=0$ triplet vector of the spin-$\tfrac12$ factor, and let
$$\Phi_-:=(\varphi_-\otimes\chi_+),\qquad \varphi_-:=(u\otimes v-v\otimes u)/\sqrt2,$$
$$\Phi_+:=(\varphi_+\otimes\chi_-),\qquad \varphi_+:=(u\otimes v+v\otimes u)/\sqrt2,$$
be the two declared antisymmetric sector vectors, with $\rho_\pm:=T_{\Phi_\pm,\Phi_\pm}$
the corresponding declared sector preparations. Then:

(a) *declared preparations*: $\Phi_\pm$ are unit vectors of the antisymmetric
sector $\mathfrak H_2^-$ of the model, and $\rho_\pm$ are declared sector
preparations;

(b) *mean energies*: the means of the declared energy observable in the two
preparations exist, are finite and equal
$$m_{\rho_+}(H_2^-)=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v+D+X,\qquad m_{\rho_-}(H_2^-)=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v+D-X;$$
in particular the **exchange splitting** of the two preparations is
$m_{\rho_+}-m_{\rho_-}=2X$;

(c) *repulsive-Coulomb ordering*: in the Coulomb case with $u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
one has $X\ge0$ and therefore $m_{\rho_-}(H_2^-)\le m_{\rho_+}(H_2^-)$: the
spatially antisymmetric, spin-triplet preparation has the lower mean pair
energy of the two;

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of the declared
model, the declared orbitals and the adopted spin-statistics sector of P6;
they derive no spin-statistics theorem, assert no measured energy difference,
compare no experimental spectrum, and make no claim that the declared
orbitals approximate any atomic state.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared spin-1/2 fermionic species, $N=2$, the external and pair data of the statement, the orthonormal orbitals $u,v\in W^{2,2}$, the spin vectors $\chi_\pm$ and the vectors $\Phi_\pm$.

[F1] **Tensor square and sectors.** The completed tensor square $K\widehat\otimes K$ of the spin-spatial one-particle space $K=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^2)$ has the pairing of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (b), $\|x\otimes y\|=\|x\|\|y\|$; the exchange unitary $U_{(12)}$ and the projections $P_\pm^{(2)}$ satisfy $P_+^{(2)}=\frac12(I+U_{(12)})$, $P_-^{(2)}=\frac12(I-U_{(12)})$, and $U_{(12)}(x\otimes y)=y\otimes x$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F2] **Euclidean product unitary.** The map $u\otimes v\mapsto u(x)v(y)$ extends to a surjective linear isometry $\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)\widehat\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3)\to L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]).

[F3] **Slot operators and the pair interaction.** For bounded $S,T\in\mathcal B(L^2(\mathbb R^3))$ the operators $S\otimes I$ and $I\otimes T$ are bounded with the elementary-tensor action of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a); the pair multiplier $M_W$ of the math supplier acts on the spatial factors and as the identity on spin, and for orthonormal spatial $u,v$ the spatial expectations of $M_W$ in $\varphi_\pm$ are $D\pm X$ with $D,X$ as displayed ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]] clause (c)); in the Coulomb case $D,X$ are finite, $D\ge0$, $X\ge0$, and the vectors lie in $D(M_W)$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]] clause (d)).

[F4] **Sector self-adjointness and domain.** In the bounded case the operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=K+M_W$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$ is self-adjoint with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] clauses (b), (c)); in the Coulomb case with bounded $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ it is self-adjoint with the same domain ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]] clauses (b), (c)); the transported antisymmetric projection reduces it, and the restriction $H_2^-$ is self-adjoint on the sector ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] clause (e)).

[F5] **Sobolev tensor bound.** If $u,v\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ then $u\otimes v\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$: with the $L^1$ Fourier transform and Plancherel ([[thm-plancherel]], [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]), $(1+|\xi|^2+|\eta|^2)\le(1+|\xi|^2)+(1+|\eta|^2)$ and Fubini give $\|u\otimes v\|_{W^{2,2}}\le2\|u\|_{W^{2,2}}\|v\|_{L^2}+2\|u\|_{L^2}\|v\|_{W^{2,2}}$.

[F6] **Moments.** For a unit vector $\psi$ in the domain of a self-adjoint $A$, the mean of the outcome law in the pure preparation of $\psi$ equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clause (a), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; exhibit the two sector vectors, split the energy expectation into its one-body and pair parts using spin independence, and insert the supplied direct and exchange integrals.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [The declared preparations are unit sector vectors] The spin vectors $\chi_\pm$ are unit vectors of $\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2$ with $U_{(12)}\chi_+=\chi_+$ and $U_{(12)}\chi_-=-\chi_-$, and $\varphi_\pm\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)\widehat\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ are unit vectors with $U_{(12)}\varphi_+=\varphi_+$, $U_{(12)}\varphi_-=-\varphi_-$ by [F1] and the symmetry relations $u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u$; hence $U_{(12)}(\varphi_\pm\otimes\chi_\mp)=-(\varphi_\pm\otimes\chi_\mp)$, so $\Phi_\pm$ lie in the antisymmetric sector and are unit vectors by [F1], [F2]. This proves (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Domain membership and the one-body expectation] Both $u$ and $v$ lie in $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, so $u\otimes v$ and $v\otimes u$ lie in $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$ by [F5]; tensoring with the smooth spin vectors and transporting by $\Theta$ and the spin identification places $\Phi_\pm$ in the domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$ of $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ of [F4]. The one-body operator $h_1+h_2$ with the declared $h$ acts as the identity on the spin factor, so by [F1] the pairing of $h_1+h_2$ with $\varphi_\pm\otimes\chi_\mp$ equals the spatial pairing with $\varphi_\pm$; expanding the two terms of $\varphi_\pm$ and using orthonormality gives $\langle(h_1+h_2)\varphi_\pm,\varphi_\pm\rangle=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v$ for both signs. [F1, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 [The pair expectation and the mean energies] The pair multiplier $M_W$ is the identity on spin and symmetric in the two spatial slots, so its pairing with $\Phi_\pm$ equals its spatial pairing with $\varphi_\pm$, which is $D\pm X$ by [F3]; combined with [F1] and step 1.2 the mean energies are $m_{\rho_\pm}(H_2^-)=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v+D\pm X$, the means being finite and given by [F6] because $\Phi_\pm$ lie in the domain of $H_2^-$ by step 1.2 and [F4]. This proves (b). [F1, F3, F4, F6, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [The repulsive ordering] In the Coulomb case $u,v\in W^{1,2}$ and [F3] clause (d) gives $D\ge0$ and $X\ge0$; therefore $m_{\rho_+}-m_{\rho_-}=2X\ge0$ by step 2.1, so the spatially antisymmetric spin-triplet preparation has the lower mean pair energy. This proves (c). [F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a), step 2.1 proves (b) and step 3.1 proves (c). Every quantity is a mean in the declared model and the declared orbitals; the spin-statistics association is the adopted sector of P6 and no measured or atomic energy entered, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **What the exchange term is.** $X$ is the integral of the overlap density $\overline uv$ against its translate; it is not an interaction between distinguishable particles, and its sign in the repulsive-Coulomb case is the content of clause (c). The theorem compares two declared preparations of the same model; it does not claim that a many-electron ground state is either of them.
- **Bounded versus Coulomb.** The bounded case relies on the elementary expectation identity of the math supplier and requires only $u,v\in W^{2,2}$; the Coulomb case additionally uses the Hardy-type bound of that supplier to make $D$ and $X$ finite and to obtain $X\ge0$.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 10.1-10.2 printed pages 229-235 (PDF pages 237-243): the symmetric and antisymmetric electron-pair spatial functions, the direct and exchange integrals D and E of the pair interaction, the singlet-triplet ordering and the perturbative helium estimates

R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Chapter 6 'Multi-Particle Systems', Sections 6.4-6.5 printed pages 88-92 (PDF pages 87-91): two-particle systems with the centre-of-mass and reduced-mass separation, the symmetry requirement on identical-particle wavefunctions and the overlap-dependent exchange correction to the pair probability

items.title: The canonical preparation as the unique free-energy minimiser of the declared finite-sector model
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] together with the
state, probability, dynamics and preparation postulates P1, P2, P4, P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-dimensional sector class of the entropy definition: the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] has sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ of finite dimension $D\ge1$ with self-adjoint energy
operator $H_N^\sigma$, assigned temperature $T>0$, inverse temperature
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ and eigen-decomposition
$H_N^\sigma=\sum_{j=1}^DE_jT_{v_j,v_j}$ with orthonormal eigenbasis
$(v_1,\dots,v_D)$ and real eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_D$. Write
$q_j:=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N$ with $Z_N:=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$,
$\rho_\beta:=\sum_jq_jT_{v_j,v_j}$, and let
$F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho)$ and
$F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-k_BT\log Z_N$ be the free-energy functional and
equilibrium free energy of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] clauses (e).
Then:

(a) *the canonical preparation*: $Z_N\in(0,\infty)$ is a finite sum,
$q_j>0$, $\sum_jq_j=1$, and $\rho_\beta$ is a declared sector preparation of
the model with
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)=\frac1{Z_N}\sum_{j=1}^DE_je^{-\beta E_j},\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z_N+\beta\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma);$$

(b) *free-energy minimum*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ one
has $F(\rho)\ge F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_BT\log Z_N$;

(c) *uniqueness*: equality $F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$ holds if and only if
$\rho=\rho_\beta$; consequently the canonical preparation is the unique
minimiser of the free-energy functional over the declared sector
preparations, and $F(\rho_\beta)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$;

(d) *degenerate case*: if $H_N^\sigma=c\,\mathrm{id}$ for a real $c$, then
$Z_N=De^{-\beta c}$, $\rho_\beta=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$,
$s(\rho_\beta)=\log D$ and $F_{\mathrm{eq}}=c-k_BT\log D$;

(e) *scope*: the statement is conditional on the adopted ensemble postulate
and on the declared finite-dimensional model; it asserts no equilibration of
any preparation towards $\rho_\beta$, no rate of approach, no thermodynamic
limit, no pressure or volume variable, and, for a laboratory sample, it
inherits the tested identification of the preparation and temperature
assignment of P7.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared finite-dimensional sector model with energy operator $H_N^\sigma$, eigen-decomposition and parameters $\beta$, $T$, $k_B$; the canonical preparation $\rho_\beta$ and the functional $F$ of the statement.

[F1] **Supplied finite Gibbs data.** For the finite-dimensional self-adjoint $H_N^\sigma$ with eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_D$ and orthonormal eigenbasis $(v_1,\dots,v_D)$, and $\beta>0$: $Z_N=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}\in(0,\infty)$, $\rho_\beta\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)=Z_N^{-1}\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}E_j$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$, and for every density operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)\ge-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$ with $s(\rho)\le\log D$ and equality $s(\rho)=\log D$ exactly for $\rho=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F2] **Spectral decomposition of a preparation.** A density operator $\rho$ on the finite-dimensional space $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ has the form $\rho=\sum_{i=1}^Dw_iT_{u_i,u_i}$ with $w_i\ge0$, $\sum_iw_i=1$ and $(u_i)$ an orthonormal eigenbasis, by [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]] and [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] applied as in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a); with $p_{ij}:=|\langle u_i,v_j\rangle|^2$ one has $\sum_jp_{ij}=1$ and $\sum_ip_{ij}=1$, because $(u_i)$ and $(v_j)$ are orthonormal bases.

[F3] **Logarithm and Jensen.** $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is strictly increasing and concave and satisfies the scalar inequality $x\log x-xy\ge x-e^{y}$ for all $x>0$, $y\in\mathbb R$, with equality exactly for $x=e^{y}$ ([[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]], [[thm-finite-jensen-inequality]]); for the probability vector $r_i=\sum_jp_{ij}q_j>0$ one has $\sum_ip_{ij}\log q_j\le\log r_i$, and $\sum_iw_i\log(w_i/r_i)\ge\sum_i(w_i-r_i)=0$ with equality exactly when $w_i=r_i$ for every $i$ with $w_i>0$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compare the free-energy functional with its value at the Gibbs operator by an eigenvalue computation over the two orthonormal bases, using the scalar logarithm inequality and Jensen's inequality.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [The canonical preparation and its data] By [F1], $Z_N=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ is a finite sum with $0<Z_N<\infty$; since $D\ge1$ each term is positive, so $q_j=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N>0$ with $\sum_jq_j=1$. By [F1] the operator $\rho_\beta=\sum_jq_jT_{v_j,v_j}$ is a density operator on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, hence a declared sector preparation of the model, and the two displayed identities are the clauses of [F1] together with the entropy definition. This proves (a). [F1, algebra]

1.2 [The free-energy difference] Let $\rho=\sum_iw_iT_{u_i,u_i}$ be a declared sector preparation as in [F2], and write $p_{ij}=|\langle u_i,v_j\rangle|^2$, $r_i=\sum_jp_{ij}q_j>0$. Computing in the eigenbasis of $H_N^\sigma$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)=\sum_{i,j}w_ip_{ij}E_j$ and $s(\rho)=-\sum_iw_i\log w_i$; since $q_j=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N$ gives $\beta E_j=-\log q_j-\log Z_N$, one has $\beta\bigl(F(\rho)-F_{\mathrm{eq}}\bigr)=\beta\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-s(\rho)+\log Z_N=\sum_iw_i\sum_jp_{ij}\bigl(\log w_i-\log q_j\bigr)$, where the terms involving $\log Z_N$ cancel by [F2] and $\sum_iw_i=1$. By [F3] the inner sum is at least $\log w_i-\log r_i$, so $\beta(F(\rho)-F_{\mathrm{eq}})\ge\sum_iw_i\log(w_i/r_i)\ge0$, and $F(\rho)\ge F_{\mathrm{eq}}$; since $\beta>0$ this proves (b). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.3 [The degenerate case] If $H_N^\sigma=c\,\mathrm{id}$ then $E_j=c$ for all $j$ and [F1] gives $Z_N=De^{-\beta c}$, $q_j=D^{-1}$, $\rho_\beta=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$; by [F1] $s(\rho_\beta)=\log D$ and $F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_BT\log(De^{-\beta c})=c-k_BT\log D$. This proves (d). [F1, algebra]

2.1 [Equality forces the canonical preparation] If $F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}$, then both inequalities of step 1.2 are equalities. Equality in $\sum_iw_i\log(w_i/r_i)\ge0$ forces $w_i=r_i$ for every $i$ with $w_i>0$ by [F3]; equality in the Jensen step forces $q_j=r_i$ for every $j$ with $p_{ij}>0$, again by [F3]. Hence whenever $p_{ij}>0$ one has $q_j=w_i$, so $u_i$ is orthogonal to every eigenspace of $\rho_\beta$ whose eigenvalue differs from $w_i$: writing $P_\lambda$ for the spectral projection of $\rho_\beta$ at $\lambda$, $\|(I-P_{w_i})u_i\|^2=\sum_{j:\,q_j\ne w_i}p_{ij}=0$. Therefore each $u_i$ lies in the eigenspace $\operatorname{ran}P_{w_i}$ of $\rho_\beta$, and $\rho=\sum_iw_iT_{u_i,u_i}=\sum_\lambda\lambda P_\lambda=\rho_\beta$, since the $u_i$ with weight $w_i=\lambda$ form an orthonormal basis of that eigenspace. Conversely $\rho=\rho_\beta$ gives equality by [F1]. Together with step 1.2 this proves (c). [F1, F2, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Conclusion and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a), steps 1.2-2.1 prove (b) and (c), and step 1.3 proves (d). The argument is an optimisation inside the declared finite-dimensional sector at the adopted ensemble parameters; no equilibration, rate, thermodynamic limit or measured thermal quantity entered, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why the minimiser is unique.** The equality analysis shows that a minimiser must be diagonal in the same eigenbasis with the same weights; it excludes the block-diagonal counterexample in which $\rho$ is diagonal in a different basis, because equal weights on a degenerate eigenspace reassemble the same projector.
- **The adopted part.** The minimum property is a theorem about the functional; that a physical sample is described by $\rho_\beta$ remains the adopted assumption of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]], not a consequence of the optimisation.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.4 printed pages 129-131 (PDF pages 137-139): the Gibbs distribution as the maximum-entropy distribution for given internal energy, U = Tr(H rho), s = beta U + ln Z (6.97), S = k_B s (6.98) and F = -k_B T ln Z (6.99)

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.4 printed pages 14-15: the maximal-entropy derivation of the Gibbs distribution, the free energy F = -T ln Z and the relations F = E - T S, S = -dF/dT

items.title: Thermal occupation means of the declared free-mode models: Bose and Fermi factors, product convergence and dilute remainders
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for the mode models
declared below, the state and probability postulates P1, P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]], and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]); assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Temperatures are assigned as in
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], so that
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$. Then:

(a) *single bosonic mode*: let $F(\mathbb C)$ be the one-mode Fock space with
number operator $N$ and orthonormal number basis $(e_n)$
([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]]), let
$\varepsilon>0$ and let the model declare the energy operator $H:=\varepsilon N$
on $F(\mathbb C)$; the model's canonical preparation at temperature $T$ is
$\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z$ with $Z=(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$, the
number readout $N$ is an assigned sharp observable with finite thermal mean
$$\langle N\rangle_\beta=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}=\frac1{e^{\varepsilon/(k_BT)}-1},$$
and all moments $\langle N^k\rangle_\beta$, $k\ge1$, are finite;

(b) *single fermionic orbital and grand-canonical shift*: on
$\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^2$ with occupation operator $N_-$ and
$\varepsilon_1,\mu\in\mathbb R$, the model's canonical (grand-canonical)
preparation $F=Z^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^1e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}T_{u_k,u_k}$
has $\operatorname{tr}F=1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}$ and occupation mean
$$\langle N_-\rangle=\frac1{e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1};$$
the same formula is the model's thermal mean when $\mu=0$ and
$\varepsilon_1>0$;

(c) *countably many independent modes*: let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$
and $\mu\in\mathbb R$, and let the model declare the free-mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ (one mode case of clause (a)) with the product reading of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]]; then the
bosonic product partition is finite exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$ and $\mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j$, and
the fermionic product partition is finite exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$; in the finite cases the products
equal $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)})^{-1}$ and
$\prod_j(1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)})$ respectively;

(d) *dilute remainders*: for $q=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon-\mu)}$ the model's
occupation means satisfy the exact identities
$$\frac q{1-q}=q+\frac{q^2}{1-q}\quad(\text{bosonic},\ 0<q<1),\qquad \frac q{1+q}=q-\frac{q^2}{1+q}\quad(\text{fermionic},\ q>0),$$
so both differ from $q$ by at most $q^2/(1-q)$ and $q^2/(1+q)$
respectively;

(e) *scope*: clauses (a)-(d) are conditional statements about the declared
mode models together with the adopted ensemble assignment; they assert no
thermodynamic limit, no continuum of radiation modes, no Bose-Einstein
condensation, no measured occupation number, and no thermalisation of a
sample. All numerical equalities are exact identities of the declared
finite-mode (or product) models at the assigned temperature.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the mode models of the statement with their energies, the assigned temperature $T$ and inverse temperature $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, and the adopted canonical preparations.

[F1] **One-mode bosonic calculation.** For $\omega>0$ and $\beta>0$, on the one-mode Fock space with number operator $N$ and orthonormal basis $(e_n)$, the bounded operator $G_\beta e_n=e^{-\beta\omega n}e_n$ is positive with $Z(\beta)=\operatorname{tr}G_\beta=(1-e^{-\beta\omega})^{-1}$, $\rho_\beta=G_\beta/Z(\beta)$ is a density operator, $\langle N\rangle_\beta=1/(e^{\beta\omega}-1)$, and $\sum_nn^ke^{-\beta\omega n}<\infty$ for every $k\ge1$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[F2] **Fermionic and grand-canonical formulas.** For $\beta>0$, $(\varepsilon_j)\subseteq(0,\infty)$ and $\mu\in\mathbb R$, with $q_j=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)}$: the two-dimensional occupation operator $N_-$ on $\mathbb C^2$ has $Z=1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}$ and mean occupancy $1/(e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1)$; the products $Z_{\mathrm B}=\sup_N\prod_{j\in N}(1-q_j)^{-1}$ and $Z_{\mathrm F}=\sup_N\prod_{j\in N}(1+q_j)$ are finite exactly under the stated summability and positivity conditions; and the single-mode dilute identities and remainder bounds hold, all as statements about diagonal weights ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fermion-and-dilute-grand-canonical-formulas]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F3] **Countable-mode product criterion.** For a separable $H$ with countable orthonormal family $(e_j)$ and weights $e^{-\beta\lambda_I}$ over finite multisets, the diagonal operator $D_\beta$ is trace class exactly when $\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$, with trace $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j})^{-1}$ in the finite case ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]] clauses (b), (d), (e)).

[F4] **Observable reading and moments.** An assigned sharp observable has outcome law $\mu^A_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$, and its mean in a pure or mixed preparation is the corresponding spectral sum when finite; the number operator $N$ is self-adjoint on its domain with $Ne_n=ne_n$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]], [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the supplied one-mode, fermionic and product calculations at the declared energies and read the occupation operators as assigned observables.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [The single bosonic mode] Apply [F1] with $\omega=\varepsilon$: $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical preparation of the declared energy operator $\varepsilon N$, the number readout $N$ is self-adjoint with $Ne_n=ne_n$ by [F4], and its thermal mean in $\rho_\beta$ equals the absolutely convergent sum $\sum_nnq^n/\sum_nq^n=1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1)$ with $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$; all higher moments are finite by [F1]. This proves (a). [F1, F4, algebra]

1.2 [The fermionic orbital and the shift] Apply [F2] at a single mode: on $\mathbb C^2$ the weights $e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}$, $k\in\{0,1\}$, give $\operatorname{tr}F=1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}$ and occupation mean $q/(1+q)=1/(e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1)$ with $q=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}$; for $\mu=0$, $\varepsilon_1>0$ this is the model's thermal mean at the declared energy $\varepsilon_1$. This proves (b) and the identities of (d). [F2, algebra]

1.3 [The product criterion] Applying the criterion [F3] to the free-mode energies with chemical-potential shift and combining with the finite products of [F2] gives the stated equivalences for the bosonic and fermionic products, under the stated conditions $\mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j$ (bosons) and no further condition (fermions). This proves (c). [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Readings] In each case the occupation number is an assigned sharp observable by [F4], so the mean of its outcome law in the canonical preparation is the number computed in steps 1.1-1.3; the identification of the computed parameters with a physical temperature and chemical potential is the adopted assumption of the ensemble postulate, and no convergence statement beyond the displayed criteria is asserted. This gives the readings of (a)-(d). [F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1-1.3 and 2.1 prove (a)-(d). The argument is a finite-mode or product computation at assigned temperature; no thermodynamic limit, continuum of modes, condensation or measured occupation entered, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **No continuum claim.** The product criterion covers countably many discrete modes; a continuum of radiation modes has divergent free partition function by the cited one-particle non-compactness argument, so a finite-volume or cutoff model would be required before making a continuum thermal claim.
- **The chemical potential.** $\mu$ is an assigned model parameter in joules with its uncertainty; the bosonic condition $\varepsilon_j-\mu>0$ is required for each geometric factor, while the fermionic factors are finite for every real $\mu$.

items.title: Unitary evolution preserves entropy and cannot produce the canonical preparation from a different one
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], the state postulate P1
and the observable postulate P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], and adopt the
canonical equilibrium-ensemble postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for the canonical
preparation $\rho_\beta$; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in the
finite-sector class of the entropy definition: the declared model has
finite-dimensional sector space $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, self-adjoint energy
operator $H_N^\sigma$ with flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$, and every declared sector preparation
evolves as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^*$ under P4 clause (iii). Then:

(a) *entropy is conserved*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho(0)$
of the model and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$s(\rho(t))=s(\rho(0));$$

(b) *the canonical preparation is stationary*:
$U(t)\rho_\beta U(t)^*=\rho_\beta$ for every $t$, and every thermal mean
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)$ of an assigned observable is time
independent;

(c) *no unitary production of the canonical preparation*: if
$\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$ then $\rho(t)\ne\rho_\beta$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$;
equivalently, no evolution of this isolated model maps a non-canonical
declared preparation to the canonical one at any time;

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) concern the model's exact unitary flow in the
finite-sector class and the adopted canonical preparation. They assert
nothing about open systems or environment coupling, about the time behaviour
of individual readouts or their time averages, about an approach of any
readout to a thermal value in a limit, about environments or measurement
models, and about any laboratory sample; in particular clause (c) is not a
claim that no physical system ever approaches thermal equilibrium, but the
statement that the model's P4 dynamics alone does not do so.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared finite-sector model with self-adjoint $H_N^\sigma$, flow $U(t)$, canonical preparation $\rho_\beta$ of the ensemble postulate, and a declared sector preparation $\rho(0)$ with $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^*$.

[F1] **Unitary flow and density evolution.** $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ is a strongly continuous unitary group with $U(t)^*=U(t)^{-1}$ and $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, and $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^*$ is a density operator for every $t$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (b), (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

[F2] **Spectral decomposition and entropy.** Every density operator $\rho$ on the finite-dimensional $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ has an orthonormal eigenbasis $(u_i)$ with eigenvalues $w_i\ge0$, and $s(\rho)=-\sum_{i:w_i>0}w_i\log w_i$ depends only on the eigenvalue multiset ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]], [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] clause (b), [[def-natural-logarithm]]).

[F3] **Canonical preparation.** $\rho_\beta=Z_N^{-1}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$ with $Z_N=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ is diagonal in an orthonormal eigenbasis $(v_j)$ of $H_N^\sigma$ with strictly positive weights $q_j=Z_N^{-1}e^{-\beta E_j}$, and it is a declared sector preparation ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a), [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] clause (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compare eigenvalue multisets under unitary conjugation and use that $\rho_\beta$ is a spectral function of the generator.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Entropy conservation] Let $\rho(0)=\sum_iw_iT_{u_i,u_i}$ be the spectral decomposition of [F2]. By [F1], $U(t)$ is unitary, so $(U(t)u_i)$ is an orthonormal basis and $\rho(t)=\sum_iw_iT_{U(t)u_i,U(t)u_i}$: the eigenvalues of $\rho(t)$ are the same $w_i$ with the same multiplicities. By [F2] the entropy depends only on that multiset, so $s(\rho(t))=s(\rho(0))$ for every $t$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Stationarity of the canonical preparation] By [F3] $\rho_\beta$ is diagonal in the eigenbasis $(v_j)$ of $H_N^\sigma$; the same basis diagonalizes $U(t)$ with eigenvalues $e^{-itE_j/\hbar}$, so $U(t)T_{v_j,v_j}U(t)^*=T_{v_j,v_j}$ for every $j$ and hence $U(t)\rho_\beta U(t)^*=\rho_\beta$. Every thermal mean $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)$ is therefore time independent by [F1]. This proves (b). [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 [No unitary production of the canonical preparation] Suppose $\rho(t)=\rho_\beta$ for some $t$. Applying the unitary $U(t)^*$ on both sides and using $U(t)^*=U(t)^{-1}$ from [F1], $\rho(0)=U(t)^*\rho_\beta U(t)=\rho_\beta$ by step 1.2 applied to $-t$. Hence $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$ implies $\rho(t)\ne\rho_\beta$ for every $t$, which is (c). [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1-2.1 prove (a)-(c). The argument used only the unitary flow, the eigenvalue multiset of a preparation and the spectral form of $\rho_\beta$; no environment, measurement model, readout equilibration or laboratory sample entered, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Entropy versus readout equilibration.** Clause (a) constrains the entropy of the full sector preparation; it does not prevent the outcome law of a chosen readout from approaching a stationary average under the flow. Clause (c) is the sharp statement about the preparation itself.
- **Open systems.** The theorem does not apply to a reduced description obtained by tracing out an environment; such a description requires its own model assumption, as P4 clause (v) records.

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.1 printed page 12: the Liouville equation, its stationary solutions commuting with H, and the remark that the von Neumann entropy is conserved under the Liouville dynamics

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the many-body and equilibrium models
items.statement:
## Recorded scope

The page declares and works with the finite-mode and spatial realizations of a
**declared fixed-$N$ many-body model**
([[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]): a species sector of
P6, a one-particle energy operator, a pair interaction and the self-adjoint
restriction of the labelled Hamiltonian to the adopted symmetric or
antisymmetric sector. Everything proved on the page is a conditional
statement about such a declared model at declared parameters:

- the non-interacting finite-mode model is diagonal in the occupation basis
  with the stated occupation eigenvalues, partition sum and ground energy
  ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-noninteracting-sector-diagonalization]]);
- the one-body readout of a bounded self-adjoint one-particle quantity has
  mean equal to $N$ times the pairing of the one-body reduced preparation
  with that quantity ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-one-body-readout-law]]);
- for two orthonormal orbitals and a repulsive Coulomb pair interaction the
  spatially antisymmetric (spin-triplet) sector preparation has the lower
  mean pair energy, with splitting the exchange integral
  ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-exchange-energy-splitting]]);
- in the finite-sector class the canonical preparation is the unique
  minimiser of the free-energy functional at the assigned
  $\beta=1/(k_BT)$ ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-equilibrium-characterization]]),
  and the free-mode thermal occupation means are the Bose and Fermi factors
  with the stated product convergence criterion and dilute remainders
  ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-occupation-predictions]]);
- the model's unitary flow preserves the entropy of every declared
  preparation and never maps a preparation different from the canonical one
  to it ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-unitary-evolution-preserves-entropy]]).

## Adopted assumptions and parameters

The **canonical ensemble** is the adopted assumption of
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]; the maximum-entropy
and free-energy arguments are motivations inside the model, and the
free-energy minimum theorem is a statement about the functional, not a
derivation of the ensemble from P1-P4. The **Boltzmann constant** is the exact
SI defining constant, while the **temperature**, **chemical potential**,
masses, couplings and any potential parameters are assigned model parameters
with uncertainty ([[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]],
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]). The assignment of a concrete
sample, mode family or detector to these model objects is a tested
identification under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

## Explicitly not asserted

The page does **not** assert: thermalization or equilibration of any
preparation (the opposite conservation statement is proved for the closed
model); a thermodynamic limit, pressure, volume, phase transitions or
condensation; entropy or free energy for infinite-dimensional sectors, for
which $\rho\log\rho$ need not be trace class; any spin-statistics theorem,
which remains the adopted sector assignment of P6; any experimental value,
count or measured level splitting. The mode models are declared
idealizations: a finitely many-mode or product-of-modes reading of a free
system, not a derivation from a spatial continuum model. The exchange
computation of the page compares two declared preparations of one model; it
does not claim that any atom's spectrum equals the difference computed.

## Source limits

The physical reading of the Gibbs distribution and of the relations among
$U$, $S$ and $F$ follows the treatments of Binney-Skinner and Burmistrov-Lunkin
at the indicated locators; both are textbook and lecture-note presentations
whose thermodynamic identifications are heuristic model assumptions rather
than mathematical derivations, and the present page therefore records them as
adopted assumptions. Burmistrov-Lunkin work with $\beta$ as a formal
inverse-energy parameter and set $k_B=1$ implicitly; the SI reading
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ with the exact BIPM value of $k_B$ used here is our own
convention, not a claim made at their locators. No source supplies measured
temperature-dependent data for the declared mode models on this page, and no
experiment item is created from these sources.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.4 printed pages 129-132 (PDF pages 137-140): the Gibbs distribution taken as the maximum-entropy distribution, the thermodynamic interpretation of Z, U, S and F, and the authors' own caution that the dependence of Z on T and V can be computed for only very few Hamiltonians

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.1 printed page 13: the remark that the von Neumann entropy is conserved under the Liouville equation, and Section 1.1.4 printed pages 14-15: the maximal-entropy motivation for the Gibbs distribution

items.title: The two-site bond model: exact canonical weights, mean energy, entropy and free energy of one particle on two sites
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P7 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], and work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] with:
one-particle space $K=\mathbb C^2$, declared sites $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$ an
orthonormal basis of $K$, particle number $N=1$, single site-occupation
sector, and the declared one-particle operator (the **bond Hamiltonian**)
$$h:=-t\bigl(T_{|1\rangle,|2\rangle}+T_{|2\rangle,|1\rangle}\bigr),\qquad t>0\ \text{in joules}.$$
Adopt the canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ and inverse temperature $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, and read
$\varepsilon:=2t$ as the tunnelling splitting. Then:

(a) $h$ has the orthonormal eigenbasis
$$u_\mp:=\frac{|1\rangle\mp|2\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad h u_\mp=\mp t\,u_\mp,$$
so its eigenvalues are $-t$ and $+t$; equivalently $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ is the
two-level Hamiltonian of
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-two-level-thermal-formulas]] with levels $0$ and
$\varepsilon=2t$ and eigenvectors $u_-,u_+$;

(b) the canonical preparation of $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ and hence of $h$ is
$$\rho_\beta=\frac{T_{u_-,u_-}+e^{-2\beta t}\,T_{u_+,u_+}}{1+e^{-2\beta t}},$$
with partition sum $Z=1+e^{-2\beta t}$;

(c) the exact means, entropy and free energy are
$$\langle h\rangle_\beta=\frac{2t}{e^{2\beta t}+1}-t=-t\tanh(\beta t),\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)+\frac{2\beta te^{-2\beta t}}{1+e^{-2\beta t}},\qquad F=-\frac1\beta\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)-t,$$
and for every $\beta>0$ one has $-t<\langle h\rangle_\beta<0$ and
$0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log2$;

(d) *scope*: the computation is an exact statement about the declared
two-dimensional bond model at the assigned temperature; it identifies no
physical double-well or molecular system, asserts no measured splitting and
no transition, and the temperature assignment is the tested identification of
P7.

## Verification

[L1] **The supplied two-level formulas.** For a two-dimensional space with
orthonormal basis $(u_0,u_1)$ and $H=\varepsilon T_{u_1,u_1}$, $\varepsilon>0$,
$\beta>0$: $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, $\rho_\beta$ is the corresponding
mixture, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\varepsilon/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)$
with values in $(0,\varepsilon/2)$, and
$s(\rho_\beta)=\log(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon})+\beta\varepsilon/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)<\log2$,
with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$
([[lem-nrqm-many-body-two-level-thermal-formulas]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[L2] **The declared model.** The finite-mode realization of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] with $K=\mathbb C^2$,
$N=1$, one-particle operator $h$ and $W=0$ is a declared non-interacting
model; its sector is $K$ itself and the canonical preparation is the Gibbs
operator of the adopted ensemble postulate; the free-energy functional is
$F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho h)-k_BT s(\rho)$ by
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] clause (e).

**Proof technique:** direct; diagonalise the two-by-two real symmetric matrix
and substitute the supplied two-level formulas with $\varepsilon=2t$ after
the shift by $t\,\mathrm{id}$.

**Given:** the declared bond model with coupling $t>0$, temperature $T>0$, $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, the vectors $u_\mp$, and [L1], [L2].

1.1 [Diagonalisation] In the basis $(|1\rangle,|2\rangle)$ the operator $h$ has the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&-t\\-t&0\end{pmatrix}$; the vectors $u_\mp=(|1\rangle\mp|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ are orthogonal unit vectors and $h u_\mp=\mp t\,u_\mp$ by direct evaluation, so $\{u_-,u_+\}$ is an orthonormal eigenbasis with eigenvalues $-t$ and $t$ by [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]. Hence $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ has the eigenvalues $0$ on $u_-$ and $2t$ on $u_+$, and it satisfies the hypothesis of [L1] with $\varepsilon=2t$, $u_0=u_-$, $u_1=u_+$. This proves (a). [L1, algebra]

2.1 [Canonical data] Applying [L1] with $\varepsilon=2t$ gives $Z=1+e^{-2\beta t}$ and $\rho_\beta=Z^{-1}(T_{u_-,u_-}+e^{-2\beta t}T_{u_+,u_+})$ for $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$; since $h=(h+t\,\mathrm{id})-t\,\mathrm{id}$ and both operators are functions of the same eigenbasis, the Gibbs operator of $h$ is the same $\rho_\beta$, because the Gibbs weights are unchanged by the shift of all levels by the constant $t$ (the explicit weights depend only on the differences of the levels). The mean of $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ is $2t/(e^{2\beta t}+1)\in(0,t)$, so $\langle h\rangle_\beta=2t/(e^{2\beta t}+1)-t=-t\tanh(\beta t)$, which lies in $(-t,0)$ because $e^{2\beta t}>1$ for $\beta t>0$; the entropy formula is that of [L1] at $\varepsilon=2t$ and satisfies $0\le s<\log2$ by [L1], and $F=-\beta^{-1}\log(1+e^{-2\beta t})-t$ is the free energy of $h$ by [L2] and [L1]. This proves (b) and (c) apart from the scope clause. [L1, L2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Scope] The computation used only the declared two-dimensional model, its exact diagonalisation and the supplied two-level formulas; no physical double well, measured splitting, transition or thermodynamic limit entered, which is (d). [L1, L2, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **The shift by $t\,\mathrm{id}$.** Adding a constant to the Hamiltonian
  multiplies $Z$ by an exponential and leaves the canonical preparation and
  the entropy unchanged while shifting the free energy by the same constant;
  the example uses this to instantiate the supplied two-level formulas, whose
  levels are $0$ and $\varepsilon$.
- **Low- and high-temperature values.** The formulas give $s\to0$ and
  $\langle h\rangle_\beta\to-t$ as the exponential factor is suppressed, and
  $s\to\log2$, $\langle h\rangle_\beta\to0$ as it approaches one; the
  example states the exact formulas and the bounds, not a limit theorem.

items.title: Finite-mode non-interacting thermal ensembles: two fermions in three modes and two bosons in two modes
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt P1, P2 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]], and adopt the
canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ with $\beta=1/(k_BT)$. Fix $\varepsilon>0$ in joules.

**Fermionic model.** One-particle space $K=\mathbb C^3$ with modes
$f_1,f_2,f_3$, fermionic statistics $\sigma=-$, $N=2$, and the declared
one-particle operator $h:=\varepsilon\,(0\cdot T_{f_1,f_1}+1\cdot T_{f_2,f_2}+2\cdot T_{f_3,f_3})$.

**Bosonic model.** One-particle space $K=\mathbb C^2$ with modes $g_1,g_2$,
bosonic statistics $\sigma=+$, $N=2$, and $h':=\varepsilon(0\cdot T_{g_1,g_1}+1\cdot T_{g_2,g_2})$.

Then:

(a) in the fermionic model the antisymmetric sector has orthonormal
eigenbasis $e_{\{1,2\}}^\wedge,e_{\{1,3\}}^\wedge,e_{\{2,3\}}^\wedge$ with
energies $\varepsilon,2\varepsilon,3\varepsilon$; the partition sum and the
exact occupation means are
$$Z_{\mathrm F}=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-3\beta\varepsilon},$$
$$\langle N_1\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm F}},\quad \langle N_2\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-3\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm F}},\quad \langle N_3\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-3\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm F}},$$
with $\langle N_1+N_2+N_3\rangle_\beta=2$ and ground energy
$\varepsilon$ (configuration $\{1,2\}$);

(b) in the bosonic model the symmetric sector has orthogonal eigenbasis
$m_{(2,0)},m_{(1,1)},m_{(0,2)}$ with energies $0,\varepsilon,2\varepsilon$;
the partition sum and the exact occupation means are
$$Z_{\mathrm B}=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+e^{-2\beta\varepsilon},\qquad \langle N_1\rangle_\beta=\frac{2+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm B}},\qquad \langle N_2\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+2e^{-2\beta\varepsilon}}{Z_{\mathrm B}},$$
with $\langle N_1+N_2\rangle_\beta=2$ and ground energy $0=N\varepsilon_1$;

(c) *scope*: the computations are exact statements about the declared
finite-mode models at the assigned temperature; they assert no physical
species, no measured occupation, no thermalisation and no thermodynamic
limit.

## Verification

[L1] **Diagonalisation theorem.** In the non-interacting finite-mode model
the labelled operator $\sum_ih^{(i)}$ is diagonal on the product basis with
eigenvalue $\sum_k\varepsilon_{i_k}$, the Slater vectors $e_J^\wedge$ and the
symmetric vectors $m_\lambda$ are eigenvectors of the sector operator with
eigenvalues $\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j$ and $\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j$,
and the partition sum is the corresponding finite sum
([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-noninteracting-sector-diagonalization]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[L2] **Occupation operators.** The occupation operators $N_j$ act on the
sector basis by $N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)e_J^\wedge$ and
$N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_jm_\lambda$, and the sector dimensions are two in the
bosonic and three in the fermionic case; the occupations are assigned sharp
observables with finite means in every preparation
([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clauses (c), (d),
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a),
(b), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]]).

**Proof technique:** direct; list the occupation configurations, read their
energies from the diagonalisation theorem, and compute the weighted means in
the canonical weights.

**Given:** the declared fermionic and bosonic finite-mode models, the energies $0,\varepsilon,2\varepsilon$, the assigned temperature data $\beta>0$, and [L1], [L2].

1.1 [Fermionic configuration sum] The two-element subsets of $\{1,2,3\}$ are $\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\}$ with energies $0+\varepsilon=\varepsilon$, $0+2\varepsilon=2\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon+2\varepsilon=3\varepsilon$ by [L1]; the canonical weights are $q_J=e^{-\beta\lambda_J}/Z_{\mathrm F}$, and the occupation means are $\sum_Jq_J\mathbf 1_J(j)$ by [L2], giving the three displayed formulas. The total occupation is $\sum_Jq_J\cdot2=2$ because every configuration has two occupied modes, and the smallest energy is that of $\{1,2\}$, namely $\varepsilon$, by [L1] clause (c). This proves (a). [L1, L2, algebra]

1.2 [Bosonic configuration sum] The occupation vectors of total two in two modes are $(2,0),(1,1),(0,2)$ with energies $0,\varepsilon,2\varepsilon$ by [L1]; the canonical weights are $q_\lambda=e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}/Z_{\mathrm B}$ and the occupation means are $\sum_\lambda q_\lambda\lambda_j$ by [L2], giving $\langle N_1\rangle=(2\cdot1+1\cdot e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+0)/Z_{\mathrm B}$ and $\langle N_2\rangle=(0+1\cdot e^{-\beta\varepsilon}+2\cdot e^{-2\beta\varepsilon})/Z_{\mathrm B}$, and the total occupation is $2$ because every configuration has $\sum_j\lambda_j=2$; the ground energy is $0=N\varepsilon_1$ by [L1] clause (c). This proves (b). [L1, L2, algebra]

2.1 [Checks and scope] In both models $Z$ is a finite sum of positive terms, hence $0<Z<\infty$; the displayed occupation sums equal the particle number $N=2$ identically in $\beta$ by steps 1.1-1.2, and the ground energies agree with the general formulas of [L1] clause (c) for the sorted energy lists $(0,\varepsilon,2\varepsilon)$ and $(0,\varepsilon)$. Every quantity is a spectral datum of the declared finite-dimensional model; no physical species, measured occupation, thermalisation or thermodynamic limit entered, which is (c). [L1, L2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Dimension counts.** The fermionic sector is three-dimensional by exclusion and the bosonic sector is three-dimensional by the configuration count; the two examples are therefore directly comparable finite checks of the diagonalisation theorem at different statistics.
- **Exactness.** The formulas are exact rational functions of $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$; no expansion in $\varepsilon/(k_BT)$ is used, and the dilute-limit approximations are treated separately on this page.

items.title: Free-mode statistics at low occupation: exact dilute identities, a finite arithmetic check and two convergence examples
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the mode models and thermal readings of
[[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-occupation-predictions]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ with $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, and put $x:=\beta\varepsilon>0$ and
$q:=e^{-x}\in(0,1)$ for a single mode of energy $\varepsilon>0$ (or, in the
grand-canonical reading, $x=\beta(\varepsilon-\mu)$ with $q=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon-\mu)}$).
Then:

(a) the exact single-mode means and their dilute identities are
$$\langle N\rangle_{\mathrm B}=\frac{q}{1-q}=q+\frac{q^2}{1-q},\qquad \langle N\rangle_{\mathrm F}=\frac{q}{1+q}=q-\frac{q^2}{1+q},$$
so the bosonic mean exceeds $q$ by $q^2/(1-q)$ and the fermionic mean falls
below $q$ by $q^2/(1+q)$ exactly;

(b) at $q=1/10$ the exact means are $\langle N\rangle_{\mathrm B}=1/9$ and
$\langle N\rangle_{\mathrm F}=1/11$, and the exact identities
$1/9=1/10+1/90$ and $1/11=1/10-1/110$ verify the two remainder formulas;

(c) for the free-mode energies $\varepsilon_j=j\varepsilon$,
$j\ge1$, the sums $\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})$
converge, so the bosonic and fermionic product partitions are finite
(bosonic case with $\mu<\varepsilon$); for the constant energies
$\varepsilon_j\equiv\varepsilon$ the sum $\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}=+\infty$
diverges, so both product partitions diverge;

(d) *scope*: the identities and the check are exact statements about the
declared mode models at the assigned temperature and, where stated, chemical
potential; no measured occupation, dilute gas, thermodynamic limit or
condensation is asserted.

## Verification

[L1] **Supplied occupation formulas.** For a single bosonic mode of energy
$\varepsilon>0$ the canonical mean occupancy is $1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1)$,
for a single fermionic orbital with parameters $\varepsilon_1,\mu$ it is
$1/(e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1)$, and the dilute identities and remainder
bounds of clause (d) of the cited theorem hold with $q=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon-\mu)}$
([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-occupation-predictions]] clauses (a), (b), (d),
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fermion-and-dilute-grand-canonical-formulas]] clause (c)).

[L2] **Supplied product criterion.** Countably many free modes with energies
$\varepsilon_j>0$ have finite bosonic product partition exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$ and $\mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j$, and
finite fermionic product partition exactly when
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$
([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]] clauses (d), (e), [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-occupation-predictions]] clause (c)); the geometric series gives $\sum_{j\ge1}r^j=r/(1-r)$ for $0<r<1$ ([[thm-geometric-series]]).

**Proof technique:** direct; substitute $q=e^{-x}$ in the supplied means, evaluate the rational identities at $q=1/10$ in exact fractions, and apply the product criterion to the two energy sequences.

**Given:** the declared single-mode model with energy $\varepsilon>0$, assigned $\beta>0$, $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, the energy sequences $\varepsilon_j=j\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon_j\equiv\varepsilon$, and [L1], [L2].

1.1 [Dilute identities] With $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\in(0,1)$ the bosonic mean of [L1] is $1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1)=q/(1-q)$ and the fermionic mean is $1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)=q/(1+q)$; the algebraic identities $q/(1-q)=q+q^2/(1-q)$ and $q/(1+q)=q-q^2/(1+q)$ are exact for every $q\in(0,1)$, and the remainders $q^2/(1-q)$, $q^2/(1+q)$ are positive. This proves (a). [L1, algebra]

1.2 [The finite check at $q=1/10$] At $q=1/10$ the bosonic mean is $(1/10)/(9/10)=1/9$ and the fermionic mean is $(1/10)/(11/10)=1/11$; the remainders are $q^2/(1-q)=(1/100)/(9/10)=1/90$ and $q^2/(1+q)=(1/100)/(11/10)=1/110$, so the exact identities $1/9=1/10+1/90=10/90+1/90$ and $1/11=1/10-1/110=11/110-1/110$ hold. This proves (b). [L1, algebra]

1.3 [The two convergence examples] For $\varepsilon_j=j\varepsilon$ the sum is $\sum_{j\ge1}(e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^j=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})<\infty$ by [L2], and for the bosonic product one needs in addition $\mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j=\varepsilon$; for $\varepsilon_j\equiv\varepsilon$ every term of the sum equals $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}>0$, so the sum diverges and [L2] makes both product partitions infinite. This proves (c). [L2, algebra]

2.1 [Checks and scope] Steps 1.1-1.3 give the exact identities, the exact rational check, and the two convergence outcomes; every quantity is computed in the declared mode models at the assigned temperature, and no measured occupation, dilute gas, thermodynamic limit or condensation entered, which is (d). [L1, L2, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What the check tests.** The check confirms the two remainder identities in exact arithmetic at a fixed value of $q$; it is a finite verification of algebraic identities, not an empirical test and not a statement about any gas.
- **Two ways to fail convergence.** Constant free-mode energies have divergent product partition because infinitely many modes share the same positive weight; geometrically growing energies have finite product partition. The bosonic criterion additionally requires the chemical potential below the ground-mode energy.

items.title: A site-localised preparation of the two-site bond model never becomes canonical, and its readouts need not take their thermal means
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P7 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], work in the
**two-site bond model** of
[[ex-nrqm-many-body-two-site-bond-thermal-ensemble]] with coupling $t>0$,
sites $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$, bond Hamiltonian
$h=-t(T_{|1\rangle,|2\rangle}+T_{|2\rangle,|1\rangle})$ and eigenbasis
$u_\mp=(|1\rangle\mp|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ with $hu_\mp=\mp tu_\mp$, and adopt
the canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$, $\beta=1/(k_BT)$. Consider the hypothetical declared
preparation $\rho(0):=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}$ (the particle localised at
site $1$) evolving by $\rho(\tau)=U(\tau)\rho(0)U(\tau)^*$ with
$U(\tau)=\exp(-i\tau h/\hbar)$. Then:

(a) $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$, and for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$ one has
$\rho(\tau)\ne\rho_\beta$: the unitary evolution of the model never produces
the canonical preparation from this preparation;

(b) the site-$1$ occupation readout $P_1:=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}$ has the
exact mean
$$\langle P_1\rangle(\tau)=\cos^2\!\Bigl(\frac{t\tau}{\hbar}\Bigr),$$
and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta P_1)=1/2$; in particular
$\langle P_1\rangle(0)=1\ne1/2$, so at the initial time the readout does not
take its canonical mean;

(c) the energy readout $h$ has the constant mean
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\tau)h)=0$ for every $\tau$, while its canonical mean
is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta h)=-t\tanh(\beta t)<0$; hence the energy
readout never takes its canonical thermal value;

(d) *scope and interpretation*: the scenario is a hypothetical,
exactly-solved model deduction in one declared preparation; it shows that
agreement or disagreement of individual readout means with their canonical
values is not convergence of the preparation to the canonical one, and that
the model's P4 dynamics does not produce the canonical ensemble. It asserts
no observed equilibration or non-equilibration of a sample, no measured
occupation or energy, and no claim about environments or open systems.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared bond model with $t>0$, the canonical preparation $\rho_\beta$, the site-localised preparation $\rho(0)=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}$, the flow $U(\tau)$, and the times $\tau\in\mathbb R$.

[F1] **Spectral flow of the bond Hamiltonian.** For the assigned energy observable $h$ with distinct eigenvalues $\mp t$ and orthonormal eigenvectors $u_\mp$, the spectral projection-valued measure has the atoms $E(\{-t\})=T_{u_-,u_-}$ and $E(\{t\})=T_{u_+,u_+}$, so the flow of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b) is $U(\tau)=e^{it\tau/\hbar}T_{u_-,u_-}+e^{-it\tau/\hbar}T_{u_+,u_+}$ and maps $\psi_0=\alpha u_-+\beta u_+$ to $\alpha e^{it\tau/\hbar}u_-+\beta e^{-it\tau/\hbar}u_+$; the mean of a bounded observable in a pure preparation is $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clause (a)).

[F2] **Euler formula and parity.** For real $\theta$, $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$, $\cos(-\theta)=\cos\theta$, $\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta$, and $\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$, so $(e^{i\theta}+e^{-i\theta})/2=\cos\theta$ and $(e^{i\theta}-e^{-i\theta})/2=i\sin\theta$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]).

[F3] **Canonical data.** The canonical preparation of the bond model is $\rho_\beta=Z^{-1}(T_{u_-,u_-}+e^{-2\beta t}T_{u_+,u_+})$ with $Z=1+e^{-2\beta t}$, its mean energy is $-t\tanh(\beta t)\in(-t,0)$ for every $\beta>0$, and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta T_{u_-,u_-})\ne\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta T_{u_+,u_+})$ ([[ex-nrqm-many-body-two-site-bond-thermal-ensemble]] clauses (b), (c), [[lem-nrqm-many-body-two-level-thermal-formulas]]).

[F4] **Invariance statement.** In the finite-sector class, if $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$ then $\rho(\tau)\ne\rho_\beta$ for every $\tau$ ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-unitary-evolution-preserves-entropy]] clause (c)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; express the initial site vector in the energy eigenbasis, insert the supplied two-level flow, and compare the readout means with the canonical data.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [The evolved preparation and the site readout] With $\psi_0=|1\rangle=(u_-+u_+)/\sqrt2$, [F1] gives $\psi(\tau)=U(\tau)\psi_0=(e^{i\theta}u_-+e^{-i\theta}u_+)/\sqrt2$, where $\theta:=t\tau/\hbar$; by [F2] and $u_\mp=(|1\rangle\mp|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ this equals $\cos\theta\,|1\rangle+i\sin\theta\,|2\rangle$, a unit vector. Since $T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}=\tfrac12(I+\sigma_z)$ with $\sigma_z=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}-T_{|2\rangle,|2\rangle}$, and $\sigma_z\psi(\tau)=\cos\theta\,|1\rangle-i\sin\theta\,|2\rangle$, the site-occupation mean is $\langle P_1\rangle(\tau)=|\cos\theta|^2=\cos^2\theta=\cos^2(t\tau/\hbar)$, in particular $\langle P_1\rangle(0)=1$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Canonical means and the initial comparison] By [F3], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta h)=-t\tanh(\beta t)<0$; moreover $\rho_\beta$ is diagonal in the basis $(u_-,u_+)$ with strictly positive diagonal weights, so $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta\sigma_z)=0$ because $\sigma_z$ exchanges the two basis vectors, and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta P_1)=\tfrac12$; and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(0)P_1)=1\ne\tfrac12$, so $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$. [F3, algebra]

2.1 [The preparation is never canonical] Step 1.2 shows $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$; applying [F4] to the declared finite-sector model gives $\rho(\tau)\ne\rho_\beta$ for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$, which is (a). [F4, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 [The energy readout never takes its thermal value] Since $h$ commutes with $U(\tau)$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\tau)h)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(0)h)=\langle h\Psi,\Psi\rangle$ for $\Psi:=|1\rangle$, and this vanishes because $h\Psi=-t|2\rangle$ is orthogonal to $\Psi$; by step 1.2 the canonical mean is $-t\tanh(\beta t)<0$, so the two values never agree. This proves (c), and step 1.1 proves (b) together with the comparison of step 1.2. [F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 2.1-2.2 prove (a)-(c) for the declared hypothetical preparation. The scenario is an exact model deduction from the declared preparation, the bond Hamiltonian and the canonical data; no observed equilibration, measured readout or laboratory system entered, which is (d). [step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **What the scenario shows.** The preparation never equals the canonical
  one, yet the site-occupation readout has the same mean $1/2$ as the
  canonical preparation at the times when $\cos^2(t\tau/\hbar)=1/2$; the
  energy readout meanwhile never takes its canonical mean. Readout
  coincidence is therefore not state convergence, and different readouts
  behave differently under the same unitary flow.
- **Hypothetical status.** No apparatus, sampling or detection model is
  specified; the scenario is a conditional statement about the declared
  model, and any comparison with an experiment would require the declared
  preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7.

items.title: What the companion examples and the thought experiment establish
items.statement:
## Recorded scope

The companion items contain four conditional computations and one hypothetical
scenario in declared finite models:

- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-two-site-bond-thermal-ensemble]] solves the one-particle
  two-site bond model exactly: the tunnelling-split eigenbasis, the canonical
  weights and the exact mean energy, entropy and free energy;
- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-finite-mode-noninteracting-thermal-ensemble]] evaluates
  the canonical partition sums and occupation means of two fermions in three
  modes and two bosons in two modes, with the total-occupation identity and
  ground energies checked against the page's diagonalisation theorem;
- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-gas-statistics-dilute-limits]] verifies the exact Bose
  and Fermi dilute identities, evaluated in exact rational arithmetic at
  $q=1/10$, and contrasts the finite product partition of geometrically
  spaced mode energies with the divergent product of constant energies;
- [[texp-nrqm-many-body-two-site-no-thermalization]] shows, in one declared
  hypothetical preparation of the bond model, that the unitary evolution
  never produces the canonical preparation, that the site-occupation readout
  takes the canonical value $1/2$ at some times while differing from it at
  others, and that the energy readout never takes its canonical value.

## What they do not establish

None of these items contains measured data, a measured uncertainty, a
calibration, a sampling model or a detector model; all numbers are exact
model values in the declared finite-dimensional idealizations, and the
assignment of a physical system to any of these models is a tested
identification under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). In particular:

- the bond model is not any particular molecule, and its splitting $2t$ is an
  assigned parameter, not a measured spectroscopic value;
- the finite-mode examples are not ideal or interacting gases; they make no
  statement about a thermodynamic limit, pressure, condensation or a
  continuum of modes;
- the comparison of readout means with canonical values in the thought
  experiment is a statement about the declared preparation and the exact
  unitary flow; it is not evidence for or against thermalisation in nature,
  and the canonical ensemble remains the adopted assumption of
  [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]];
- the entropy conservation used in the thought experiment is the exact
  closed-system statement of
  [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-unitary-evolution-preserves-entropy]]; it neither
  forbids nor asserts any open-system or environment-induced behaviour.

## Source limits

The cited treatments supply the model formulas used here at the recorded
locators; they do not supply measured values for these particular finite
models, and no source is used as an empirical premise on this page. Where a
comparison with data would be attempted, the preparation, isolation,
detection and sampling models plus the uncertainty of every assigned
parameter would have to be declared and carried through, as P7 requires.
